items.title: Connectivity Verification (LVS)
items.text: Download notebook (.ipynb)

items.title: Connectivity Verification (LVS)
items.text:
Layout vs. Schematic (LVS) verification confirms that the physical layout of a circuit matches its intended connectivity. In photonic and electronic design, the schematic defines the intended connections between components, while the extracted netlist captures what was actually built in the layout.

kfnetlist provides the building blocks for a complete LVS workflow: detect opens, compare against a reference, and find geometric shorts. This guide walks through each step and shows how to interpret the results.

items.title: Verification methods
items.text: Method LVS category What it detects Requires klayout? detect_opens() Open circuit Unconnected ports, singleton nets No find_net_difference(ref) Net mismatch Missing / extra nets vs. reference No detect_shorts(l2n) Short circuit Geometric polygon overlaps between nets Yes normalize() Pre-processing Folds equivalent ports before comparison No check_connection() Port validation Geometric port-pair alignment checks Yes

items.title: Step 1 — Build the netlists
items.text:
A typical LVS flow compares two netlists:

  • Schematic netlist — the golden reference (what you intended)
  • Extracted netlist — what was actually built (from layout extraction)

Below we construct both by hand, deliberately introducing errors in the extracted netlist to demonstrate each detection method.

from kfnetlist import Netlist, NetlistPort, PortRef

# -- Schematic (golden reference) --
schematic = Netlist()
schematic.create_inst("mmi", kcl="PDK", component="mmi1x2", settings={"width": 500})
schematic.create_inst("wg1", kcl="PDK", component="straight", settings={"length": 10_000})
schematic.create_inst("wg2", kcl="PDK", component="straight", settings={"length": 10_000})

schematic.create_port("in")
schematic.create_port("out1")
schematic.create_port("out2")

schematic.create_net(NetlistPort(name="in"), PortRef(instance="mmi", port="o1"))
schematic.create_net(PortRef(instance="mmi", port="o2"), PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o1"))
schematic.create_net(PortRef(instance="mmi", port="o3"), PortRef(instance="wg2", port="o1"))
schematic.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o2"), NetlistPort(name="out1"))
schematic.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg2", port="o2"), NetlistPort(name="out2"))
schematic.sort()

print(f"Schematic: {len(schematic.nets)} nets, {len(schematic.ports)} ports")

Schematic: 5 nets, 3 ports

# -- Extracted netlist (from layout) --
# Errors introduced:
#   1. The mmi→wg2 connection is missing (open)
#   2. wg2.o1 is left dangling as a singleton net (stub)
#   3. An extra net connects wg2.o2 directly to "in" (unintended)

extracted = Netlist()
extracted.create_inst("mmi", kcl="PDK", component="mmi1x2", settings={"width": 500})
extracted.create_inst("wg1", kcl="PDK", component="straight", settings={"length": 10_000})
extracted.create_inst("wg2", kcl="PDK", component="straight", settings={"length": 10_000})

extracted.create_port("in")
extracted.create_port("out1")
extracted.create_port("out2")

extracted.create_net(NetlistPort(name="in"), PortRef(instance="mmi", port="o1"))
extracted.create_net(PortRef(instance="mmi", port="o2"), PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o1"))
# Missing: mmi.o3 → wg2.o1
extracted.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg2", port="o1"))  # singleton (dangling stub)
extracted.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o2"), NetlistPort(name="out1"))
extracted.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg2", port="o2"), NetlistPort(name="out2"))
extracted.sort()

print(f"Extracted: {len(extracted.nets)} nets, {len(extracted.ports)} ports")

Extracted: 5 nets, 3 ports

items.title: Step 2 — Pre-process with equivalent ports
items.text:
Before comparing, fold electrically-equivalent ports into canonical names using normalize(). This prevents false mismatches on components like pads where multiple pins connect to the same metal plane.

In this example neither netlist has equivalent ports, so normalize() is a no-op — but it should always be part of the workflow.

equivalent_ports = {
    # "pad": [["p1", "p2"]],  # uncomment if your design has equivalent port groups
}

schematic_norm = schematic.normalize(cell_name="top", equivalent_ports=equivalent_ports)
extracted_norm = extracted.normalize(cell_name="top", equivalent_ports=equivalent_ports)

schematic_norm.sort()
extracted_norm.sort()
print("Normalization applied")

Normalization applied

items.title: Step 3 — Detect opens
items.text:
detect_opens() inspects a single netlist for signs of incomplete wiring. It returns a dict with two keys:

  • unconnected_ports — top-level ports not referenced by any net
  • singleton_nets — nets with exactly one member (dangling stubs)
opens = extracted_norm.detect_opens()

print("Unconnected ports:", opens["unconnected_ports"])

singleton_nets = list(opens["singleton_nets"])
print(f"Singleton nets: {len(singleton_nets)}")
for net in singleton_nets:
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    print(f"  dangling: {' — '.join(members)}")

Unconnected ports: []
Singleton nets: 1
  dangling: wg2.o1

items.title: Interpreting open detection results
items.text: Result LVS meaning Severity Typical cause Unconnected port Definite open — a declared port is not wired Error Missing route to a top-level pin Singleton net Potential open — a port is wired but goes nowhere Warning Broken connection, dangling stub

items.title: Step 4 — Compare against reference
items.text:
find_net_difference(reference) compares two netlists by symmetric difference on their nets. It returns:

  • missing — nets in the reference that are absent from the extracted netlist (connections that should exist but don't)
  • extra — nets in the extracted netlist that are absent from the reference (unintended connections)
diff = extracted_norm.find_net_difference(schematic_norm)

missing = list(diff["missing"])
extra = list(diff["extra"])

print(f"Missing nets (in schematic but not in layout): {len(missing)}")
for net in missing:
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    print(f"  {' — '.join(members)}")

print(f"\nExtra nets (in layout but not in schematic): {len(extra)}")
for net in extra:
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    print(f"  {' — '.join(members)}")

Missing nets (in schematic but not in layout): 1
  mmi.o3 — wg2.o1

Extra nets (in layout but not in schematic): 1
  wg2.o1

items.title: Interpreting net differences
items.text: Result LVS meaning Severity Typical cause Missing net Open — a connection exists in the schematic but not in the layout Error Broken or missing route Extra net Unintended connection — a connection exists in the layout but not in the schematic Warning Accidental coupling, routing error

items.title: Step 5 — Detect geometric shorts (requires klayout)
items.text:
detect_shorts(l2n) finds polygon overlaps between electrically distinct nets on the same layer. This requires a completed klayout LayoutToNetlist extraction.

from kfnetlist.extract import detect_shorts

shorts = detect_shorts(l2n)

for s in shorts:
    print(f"SHORT: {s.net_a} <-> {s.net_b} on {s.layer}")
    print(f"  Overlap area: {s.overlap.area()} dbu^2")
    print(f"  Bounding box: {s.overlap.bbox()}")

items.title: ShortResult fields
items.text:
Field Type Description net_a str Name of the first net net_b str Name of the second net layer str Layer display name where the overlap occurs overlap kdb.Region The overlapping polygon region

The overlap region can be used to compute the area of the short (s.overlap.area()), get its bounding box (s.overlap.bbox()), or visualize it in klayout's layout viewer.

items.title: Filtering by layer
items.text:
Use the short_layers parameter to restrict detection to specific layers:

from klayout import db as kdb

# Only check metal layers
shorts = detect_shorts(
    l2n,
    short_layers=[kdb.LayerInfo(1, 0), kdb.LayerInfo(2, 0)],
)

items.title: Step 6 — Build a verification summary
items.text:
Aggregate all findings into a single pass/fail report.

def build_verification_summary(opens_result, diff_result, shorts=None):
    """Aggregate verification results into a structured summary."""
    n_unconnected = len(opens_result["unconnected_ports"])
    n_singletons = len(list(opens_result["singleton_nets"]))
    n_missing = len(list(diff_result["missing"]))
    n_extra = len(list(diff_result["extra"]))
    n_shorts = len(shorts) if shorts else 0

    passed = (n_unconnected == 0 and n_missing == 0 and n_shorts == 0)

    return {
        "pass": passed,
        "unconnected_ports": n_unconnected,
        "singleton_nets": n_singletons,
        "missing_nets": n_missing,
        "extra_nets": n_extra,
        "shorts": n_shorts,
    }


summary = build_verification_summary(opens, diff)

status = "PASS" if summary["pass"] else "FAIL"
print(f"VERIFICATION RESULT: {status}")
print(f"  Opens: {summary['unconnected_ports']} unconnected port(s), "
      f"{summary['singleton_nets']} singleton net(s)")
print(f"  Net differences: {summary['missing_nets']} missing, "
      f"{summary['extra_nets']} extra")
print(f"  Shorts: {summary['shorts']}")

VERIFICATION RESULT: FAIL
  Opens: 0 unconnected port(s), 1 singleton net(s)
  Net differences: 1 missing, 1 extra
  Shorts: 0

items.title: Exploring report data
items.text: The dicts returned by detect_opens() and find_net_difference() are the primary "report database" in kfnetlist. Here is how to explore them programmatically.

items.title: Iterating net members
items.text:
Each net in the missing or extra lists is a Net object that can be iterated to inspect its members:

for net in list(diff["missing"]):
    port_refs = []
    netlist_ports = []
    for m in net:
        if isinstance(m, PortRef):
            port_refs.append(f"{m.instance}.{m.port}")
        elif isinstance(m, NetlistPort):
            netlist_ports.append(m.name)
    print(f"Missing net: ports={netlist_ports}, refs={port_refs}")

Missing net: ports=[], refs=['mmi.o3', 'wg2.o1']

items.title: Classifying findings by category
items.text:
You can tag each finding with an LVS error category for structured reporting:

findings = []

for port_name in opens["unconnected_ports"]:
    findings.append({
        "category": "open",
        "severity": "error",
        "detail": f"Unconnected top-level port: {port_name}",
    })

for net in list(opens["singleton_nets"]):
    member = next(iter(net))
    label = (f"{member.instance}.{member.port}"
             if isinstance(member, PortRef) else member.name)
    findings.append({
        "category": "open",
        "severity": "warning",
        "detail": f"Singleton net (dangling stub): {label}",
    })

for net in list(diff["missing"]):
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    findings.append({
        "category": "net_mismatch",
        "severity": "error",
        "detail": f"Missing net: {' — '.join(members)}",
    })

for net in list(diff["extra"]):
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    findings.append({
        "category": "net_mismatch",
        "severity": "warning",
        "detail": f"Extra net: {' — '.join(members)}",
    })

print(f"Total findings: {len(findings)}")
for f in findings:
    print(f"  [{f['severity'].upper():7s}] {f['category']:15s} | {f['detail']}")

Total findings: 3
  [WARNING] open            | Singleton net (dangling stub): wg2.o1
  [ERROR  ] net_mismatch    | Missing net: mmi.o3 — wg2.o1
  [WARNING] net_mismatch    | Extra net: wg2.o1

items.title: Filtering by severity or category
items.text:
Since findings are plain dicts, standard Python filtering works:

errors_only = [f for f in findings if f["severity"] == "error"]
opens_only = [f for f in findings if f["category"] == "open"]

print(f"Errors: {len(errors_only)}, Opens: {len(opens_only)}")

Errors: 1, Opens: 1

items.title: Complete verification workflow
items.text:
Here is the full flow as a reusable pattern:

from kfnetlist import Netlist, NetlistPort, PortRef

def verify_connectivity(
    extracted: Netlist,
    schematic: Netlist,
    equivalent_ports: dict | None = None,
    l2n=None,
    short_layers=None,
) -> dict:
    """Run all connectivity checks and return a structured report."""
    eq = equivalent_ports or {}

    # 1. Normalize equivalent ports
    ext = extracted.normalize(cell_name="top", equivalent_ports=eq)
    sch = schematic.normalize(cell_name="top", equivalent_ports=eq)
    ext.sort()
    sch.sort()

    # 2. Detect opens in extracted netlist
    opens = ext.detect_opens()

    # 3. Compare against schematic
    diff = ext.find_net_difference(sch)

    # 4. Detect geometric shorts (if L2N available)
    shorts = []
    if l2n is not None:
        from kfnetlist.extract import detect_shorts
        shorts = detect_shorts(l2n, short_layers=short_layers)

    # 5. Build summary
    n_unconnected = len(opens["unconnected_ports"])
    n_missing = len(list(diff["missing"]))
    n_shorts = len(shorts)

    return {
        "pass": n_unconnected == 0 and n_missing == 0 and n_shorts == 0,
        "opens": opens,
        "diff": diff,
        "shorts": shorts,
        "summary": {
            "unconnected_ports": n_unconnected,
            "singleton_nets": len(list(opens["singleton_nets"])),
            "missing_nets": n_missing,
            "extra_nets": len(list(diff["extra"])),
            "shorts": n_shorts,
        },
    }

items.title: Mapping to LVS error categories
items.text: kfnetlist finding Traditional LVS category Severity Typical cause Unconnected port Open Error Missing route to a top-level pin Singleton net Open (potential) Warning Dangling stub, broken connection Missing net (vs. reference) Net mismatch / open Error Missing or broken route in layout Extra net (vs. reference) Net mismatch Warning Unintended connection, routing error ShortResult Short Error Metal overlap between distinct nets PortCheck failure DRC / port alignment Warning Misaligned or wrong-width port

items.title: Future: structured error reporting
items.text:
kfnetlist is working toward structured error reporting inspired by the elvis LVS engine. Planned capabilities include:

  • Error accumulation — collect all issues into a single result container instead of throwing on first error
  • KLayout RDB output — serialize errors with geometric markers for visualization in klayout's marker browser
  • Error filtering pipeline — deduplicate and merge transitive errors (e.g. collapse a power-rail short from hundreds of raw overlaps into one error group)
  • Named nets — give every net identity so shorts can report which nets are involved

See the contributing docs for the full roadmap.

items.title: Open Detection
items.text: kfnetlist provides two methods on Netlist for detecting open circuits — missing or incomplete connections that indicate wiring problems.

items.title: Methods
items.text: Method Returns Purpose detect_opens() dict Find unconnected ports and singleton nets in a single netlist find_net_difference(reference) dict[str, list[Net]] Find nets missing from or extra in self compared to reference

items.title: detect_opens()
items.text:
Inspects a single netlist for signs of incomplete wiring.

from kfnetlist import Netlist, NetlistPort, PortRef

nl = Netlist()
nl.create_inst("a", kcl="pdk", component="other", settings={})
nl.create_port("VDD")
nl.create_port("VSS")

# Only VDD is wired — VSS is an unconnected port
nl.create_net(
    NetlistPort(name="VDD"),
    PortRef(instance="a", port="p1"),
)

# A singleton net (only one member — dangling stub)
nl.create_net(
    PortRef(instance="a", port="p2"),
)

result = nl.detect_opens()
print("Unconnected ports:", result["unconnected_ports"])
print("Singleton nets:", len(result["singleton_nets"]))

Unconnected ports: ['VSS']
Singleton nets: 1

The returned dict has two keys:

  • unconnected_ports — a sorted list of top-level port names that are not referenced by any net.
  • singleton_nets — nets with exactly one member. A single-member net is a dangling stub that often indicates an accidental open.

items.title: find_net_difference(reference)
items.text:
Compares two netlists by symmetric difference on their nets. Returns a dict with "missing" nets (in reference but absent from self) and "extra" nets (in self but absent from reference).

schematic = Netlist()
schematic.create_inst("a", kcl="pdk", component="other", settings={})
schematic.create_inst("b", kcl="pdk", component="other", settings={})
schematic.create_port("VDD")
schematic.create_port("VSS")
schematic.create_net(NetlistPort(name="VDD"), PortRef(instance="a", port="p1"))
schematic.create_net(NetlistPort(name="VSS"), PortRef(instance="b", port="p1"))

# Extracted netlist is missing the VSS net
extracted = Netlist()
extracted.create_inst("a", kcl="pdk", component="other", settings={})
extracted.create_inst("b", kcl="pdk", component="other", settings={})
extracted.create_port("VDD")
extracted.create_port("VSS")
extracted.create_net(NetlistPort(name="VDD"), PortRef(instance="a", port="p1"))

diff = extracted.find_net_difference(schematic)
print(f"Missing nets: {len(diff['missing'])}")
for net in diff["missing"]:
    members = list(net)
    print(f"  Net members: {[str(m) for m in members]}")
print(f"Extra nets: {len(diff['extra'])}")

Missing nets: 1
  Net members: ["NetlistPort(name='VSS')", "b['p1']"]
Extra nets: 0

Net equality is based on sorted member content, so insertion order does not matter.

items.title: Typical workflow
items.text:
# 1. Check extracted netlist for internal issues
opens = extracted_nl.detect_opens()
if opens["unconnected_ports"]:
    print(f"Warning: unconnected ports: {opens['unconnected_ports']}")

# 2. Compare against schematic for net differences
diff = extracted_nl.find_net_difference(schematic_nl)
if diff["missing"]:
    print(f"Error: {len(diff['missing'])} nets missing from layout")
if diff["extra"]:
    print(f"Warning: {len(diff['extra'])} unexpected nets in layout")

items.title: Interpreting results for LVS
items.text:
The open detection results map directly to LVS error categories:

Result key LVS category Severity Meaning unconnected_ports Definite open Error A declared port has no route singleton_nets Potential open Warning A port is wired but goes nowhere

In a full LVS workflow, opens should be checked before comparing against a reference netlist — an unconnected port in the extracted netlist will also surface as a missing net in the comparison, so fixing the open fixes both findings.

def summarize_opens(opens_result):
    """Build a one-line summary from detect_opens() output."""
    n_unconnected = len(opens_result["unconnected_ports"])
    n_singletons = len(list(opens_result["singleton_nets"]))
    if n_unconnected == 0 and n_singletons == 0:
        return "PASS: no opens detected"
    parts = []
    if n_unconnected:
        parts.append(f"{n_unconnected} unconnected port(s)")
    if n_singletons:
        parts.append(f"{n_singletons} singleton net(s)")
    return f"FAIL: {', '.join(parts)}"


print(summarize_opens(result))

FAIL: 1 unconnected port(s), 1 singleton net(s)

items.title: Placement-Aware Netlists
items.text:
A plain Netlist captures connectivity: instances, nets, and ports. Some workflows — simulation setup, floorplanning, visualization — also need to know where each instance physically sits in the layout.

PlacedNetlist is a second flavor for exactly that. It is a subclass of Netlist (so all connectivity behaviour is inherited unchanged) whose instances are PlacedInstance objects. Each PlacedInstance adds:

  • cell — the placed cell's name (distinct from component, which is the factory name);
  • placement — a purely geometric Placement: origin x/y, orientation, mirror, and bbox.

Placement describes where an instance is; the cell name (what it is) lives on the instance, not inside the placement.

import json

from kfnetlist import (
    Netlist,
    NetlistPort,
    Placement,
    PlacedInstance,
    PlacedNetlist,
    PortRef,
)

items.title: Building a placed netlist directly
items.text:
PlacedNetlist.create_inst() mirrors Netlist.create_inst() with two extra trailing arguments: the placed cell name and a placement. The bounding box is a plain dict in klayout left/bottom/right/top convention (µm).

pnl = PlacedNetlist()

pnl.create_inst(
    name="wg1",
    kcl="PDK",
    component="straight_factory",  # factory / parametric-cell name
    settings={"width": 0.5},
    cell="straight",  # the actual layout cell name
    placement=Placement(
        x=0.0,
        y=0.0,
        orientation=0.0,
        mirror=False,
        bbox={"left": 0.0, "bottom": -0.25, "right": 10.0, "top": 0.25},
    ),
)

pnl.create_inst(
    name="bend1",
    kcl="PDK",
    component="bend_euler",
    cell="bend_euler",
    placement=Placement(
        x=10.0,
        y=0.0,
        orientation=90.0,
        mirror=False,
        bbox={"left": 10.0, "bottom": 0.0, "right": 15.0, "top": 5.0},
    ),
)

# Connectivity works exactly as on a plain Netlist.
pnl.create_port("o1")
pnl.create_net(NetlistPort(name="o1"), PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o1"))
pnl.create_net(PortRef(instance="wg1", port="o2"), PortRef(instance="bend1", port="o1"))
pnl.sort()

A PlacedNetlist is a Netlist, so connectivity tooling keeps working:

print("isinstance(pnl, Netlist):", isinstance(pnl, Netlist))
print("instance names:", pnl.instance_names())
print("nets:")
for net in pnl.nets:
    members = [
        f"{m.instance}.{m.port}" if isinstance(m, PortRef) else f"<{m.name}>"
        for m in net
    ]
    print("  -", " — ".join(members))

isinstance(pnl, Netlist): True
instance names: ['bend1', 'wg1']
nets:
  - <o1> — wg1.o1
  - bend1.o1 — wg1.o2

items.title: Inspecting placement
items.text:
instances returns PlacedInstance objects (cell + placement); placements is a convenience map of just the geometry, keyed by instance name.

for name, inst in pnl.instances.items():
    p = inst.placement
    print(f"{name}: cell={inst.cell!r} component={inst.component!r}")
    print(
        f"    origin=({p.x}, {p.y}) µm, orientation={p.orientation}°, mirror={p.mirror}"
    )
    print(f"    bbox={p.bbox}")

bend1: cell='bend_euler' component='bend_euler'
    origin=(10.0, 0.0) µm, orientation=90.0°, mirror=False
    bbox={'left': 10.0, 'bottom': 0.0, 'right': 15.0, 'top': 5.0}
wg1: cell='straight' component='straight_factory'
    origin=(0.0, 0.0) µm, orientation=0.0°, mirror=False
    bbox={'left': 0.0, 'bottom': -0.25, 'right': 10.0, 'top': 0.25}

items.title: Serialization
items.text:
PlacedNetlist round-trips through JSON and dicts like every other type. The cell sits alongside the connectivity fields, and placement is a nested block per instance.

d = pnl.to_dict()
print(json.dumps(d["instances"]["bend1"], indent=2))

{
  "kcl": "PDK",
  "component": "bend_euler",
  "settings": {},
  "array": {
    "na": 1,
    "nb": 1
  },
  "cell": "bend_euler",
  "placement": {
    "x": 10.0,
    "y": 0.0,
    "orientation": 90.0,
    "mirror": false,
    "bbox": {
      "left": 10.0,
      "bottom": 0.0,
      "right": 15.0,
      "top": 5.0
    }
  }
}

restored = PlacedNetlist.from_json(pnl.to_json())
assert restored.instances["bend1"].placement == pnl.instances["bend1"].placement
assert restored.instances["bend1"].cell == "bend_euler"
print("round-trip OK")

round-trip OK

items.title: Upgrading an existing netlist
items.text:
If you already have a plain Netlist (e.g. from another tool), attach placement with from_netlist(). It takes the netlist plus two name-keyed maps — placements and cells — and keeps only entries for instances that actually exist. Instances without an entry get empty defaults.

nl = Netlist()
nl.create_inst(name="mmi1", kcl="PDK", component="mmi1x2")
nl.create_port("in")
nl.create_net(NetlistPort(name="in"), PortRef(instance="mmi1", port="o1"))

placed = PlacedNetlist.from_netlist(
    nl,
    placements={
        "mmi1": Placement(
            x=2.0,
            y=1.0,
            orientation=180.0,
            mirror=True,
            bbox={"left": 0.0, "bottom": 0.0, "right": 6.0, "top": 2.0},
        )
    },
    cells={"mmi1": "mmi1x2"},
)

mmi = placed.instances["mmi1"]
assert isinstance(mmi, PlacedInstance)
print("cell:", mmi.cell, "| placement:", mmi.placement)
# Connectivity carried over unchanged.
print("nets preserved:", [list(n) == list(o) for n, o in zip(placed.nets, nl.nets)])

cell: mmi1x2 | placement: Placement(x=2, y=1, orientation=180, mirror=true)
nets preserved: [True]

items.title: From extraction
items.text:
When extracting from a layout, pass include_placement=True to extract(). Each returned value is then a PlacedNetlist instead of a Netlist, with the placed cell name and placement read from the layout for every surviving instance:

from kfnetlist.extract import extract

netlists = extract(
    cell,
    wrap_kdb_instance=lambda i: Instance(kcl=cell.kcl, instance=i),
    include_placement=True,
)
placed = netlists[cell.name]          # a PlacedNetlist
placed.instances["wg1"].placement.x   # origin x in µm
placed.instances["wg1"].cell          # the placed cell name

The default (include_placement=False) returns plain Netlist objects, identical to before — placement never changes connectivity, and is excluded from equality so LVS comparisons are unaffected.

See Extraction Overview for the full pipeline.

items.title: kfnetlist.morphnet
items.text:
A bidirectional netlist parser built on Lark, enabling translation between SPICE-family circuit netlist formats (HSPICE, Xyce, Spectre, Spectre-SPICE), Verilog-AMS and structural SystemVerilog.

All formats share a common intermediate representation defined in Protocol Buffers and wrapped with Pydantic v2 models, making it straightforward to parse, transform, and serialize netlists programmatically.

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• 7 netlist formats — HSPICE, SPICE, Xyce, Spectre, Spectre-SPICE, Verilog-AMS, SystemVerilog
  • Electrical and photonic — terminals named o1, o2, ... are waveguide terminals in every format; e1, ... and unprefixed names are electrical
  • Bidirectional — every format has both a parser and a writer
  • Common IR — all formats parse into the same Netlist model (Netlist → Circuit definitions → SubCircuit instances), which serializes to protobuf, JSON and YAML with the kfnetlist schema (circuit.proto) field names
  • Protocol Buffers — compact binary serialization for cross-language interop
  • Pydantic v2 — type-safe data models with JSON and YAML support
  • Lark grammars — each format is defined by a clean EBNF grammar

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
spectre.scs ──┐                          ┌── spectre.scs
hspice.sp  ───┤  parse_*()   write_*()   ├── hspice.sp
xyce.cir   ───┼──────────► Netlist ──────►├── xyce.cir
spice.sp   ───┤          (protobuf +      ├── spice.sp
vams.vams  ───┤           pydantic)       ├── vams.vams
netlist.sv ───┘                           └── netlist.sv
                             │
                        to_yaml / from_yaml
                             │
                          netlist.yaml

Each format follows the same internal pipeline:

raw text → preprocess → Lark grammar → parse tree → Transformer → Netlist
Netlist → Writer → formatted text

items.title: Quick Example
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.writer import write_vams

spectre_netlist = """\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
"""

netlist = parse_spectre(spectre_netlist)
print(write_vams(netlist))

Output:

module rc_lowpass (in_, out, gnd);
  inout in_, out, gnd;
  resistor #(.value(1k)) R1 (.p(in_), .n(out));
  capacitor #(.value(100p)) C1 (.p(out), .n(gnd));
endmodule

items.title: Supported Formats
items.text:
Format Parser Writer HSPICE kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser.parse_hspice kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.writer.write_hspice SPICE kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spice.parser.parse_spice kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spice.writer.write_spice Xyce kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.xyce.parser.parse_xyce kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.xyce.writer.write_xyce Spectre kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser.parse_spectre kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.writer.write_spectre Spectre-SPICE kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre_spice.parser.parse_spectre_spice kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre_spice.writer.write_spectre_spice Verilog-AMS kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.parser.parse_vams kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.writer.write_vams SystemVerilog kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.systemverilog.parser.parse_systemverilog kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.systemverilog.writer.write_systemverilog

Every parser and writer is also exported from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist. See Parsing netlist formats and Converting between formats for worked examples of each.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pip install kfnetlist

Or with uv:

uv add kfnetlist

See Getting Started for development setup instructions.

items.title: Netlist Structure
items.text:
A Netlist is the top-level container. It holds Circuit definitions, and each Circuit holds SubCircuit instances. These are the kfnetlist schema (circuit.proto) names, used unchanged in protobuf, JSON and YAML; only ports and port_name serialize as terminals and terminal_name:

Netlist
├── name: str
├── top_circuit: str
├── circuits: list[Circuit]
│   ├── name, class_name: str
│   ├── ports: list[Port]                          # schema: terminals
│   ├── parameters: list[Parameter]
│   ├── subcircuits: list[SubCircuit]
│   │   └── name, circuit_name, class_name, parameters
│   ├── connections: list[Connection]
│   ├── buses: list[Bus]
│   └── directives: list[Directive]
├── ext_circuits: list[ExternalCircuit]            # body-less definitions (resistor, mosfet, PDK cells)
├── directives: list[Directive]                    # .include, .lib, .param, ...
├── libraries: dict[str, ExternalLibrary]
└── simulation: Simulation | None                  # analyses, output requests, measurements

Files written before this naming (modules, top_module, module_references, module_name, ext_modules) still load.

items.title: Inspecting Circuits
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre

netlist = parse_spectre("""\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
""")

circuit = netlist.circuits[0]
print(circuit.name)  # "rc_lowpass"

# List port names
for port in circuit.ports:
    print(f"  {port.name} ({port.direction.name})")

# List instances
for sub in circuit.subcircuits:
    print(f"  {sub.name} -> {sub.circuit_name}")
    for param in sub.parameters:
        print(f"    {param.name} = {param.default_value}")

items.title: Inspecting Connections
items.text:
Connections are point-to-point links between port references:

for conn in circuit.connections:
    src = conn.source
    tgt = conn.target
    print(
        f"  net {conn.name}: {src.instance_name}.{src.port_name} -> "
        f"{tgt.instance_name}.{tgt.port_name}"
    )

items.title: Modifying Circuits
items.text:
kfnetlist.morphnet models are mutable Pydantic models: the builder methods (Circuit.add, Circuit.connect, Netlist.add, ...) edit them in place. To derive a modified copy without touching the original, use model_copy:

from kfnetlist.morphnet import Port, PortDirection

modified = netlist.model_copy(update={"name": "my_modified_circuit"})

modified_circuit = circuit.model_copy(
    update={
        "name": "rc_lowpass_v2",
        "ports": circuit.ports + [Port(name="extra", direction=PortDirection.INPUT)],
    }
)

items.title: Binary Serialization
items.text:
Compact binary format for storage or cross-language interop (C++, Java, Go, etc.):

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist

netlist = parse_spectre("""\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
""")

# Serialize to bytes
data = netlist.to_proto_bytes()
print(f"Binary size: {len(data)} bytes")

# Deserialize
restored = Netlist.from_proto_bytes(data)
assert restored == netlist

items.title: JSON Serialization
items.text:
json_str = netlist.to_json()
restored = Netlist.from_json(json_str)
assert restored == netlist

items.title: Simulation Data
items.text: kfnetlist.morphnet parses simulation directives (analyses, output requests, measurements) into structured models.

items.title: Parsing Simulation Statements
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser import parse_hspice
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import AnalysisKind

netlist = parse_hspice("""\
.macro inv vin vout vdd gnd
M1 vout vin vdd vdd pmos w=1u l=100n
M2 vout vin gnd gnd nmos w=500n l=100n
.eom inv
.tran 1n 10u
.print TRAN V(vout)
.end
""")

sim = netlist.simulation
print(f"Analyses: {len(sim.analyses)}")
print(f"Output requests: {len(sim.output_requests)}")

analysis = sim.analyses[0]
print(f"Kind: {analysis.kind.name}")  # TRAN
print(f"Arguments: {analysis.arguments}")  # ["1n", "10u"]

output = sim.output_requests[0]
print(f"Variables: {output.variables}")  # ["V(vout)"]

items.title: Analysis Kinds
items.text:
The AnalysisKind enum supports:

Kind Description OP Operating point DC DC sweep AC AC frequency sweep TRAN Transient analysis NOISE Noise analysis TF Transfer function SENS Sensitivity PZ Pole-zero DISTO Distortion FOUR Fourier FFT Fast Fourier Transform

items.title: FFT Example
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser import parse_hspice
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import AnalysisKind

netlist = parse_hspice("""\
.fft V(out) NP=1024 START=0 STOP=10u
.end
""")

fft = netlist.simulation.analyses[0]
assert fft.kind == AnalysisKind.FFT
print(fft.options)  # {"NP": "1024", "START": "0", "STOP": "10u"}

items.title: Preprocessing Raw Text
items.text:
Each format has a preprocessor that normalizes raw input before parsing (strips comments, joins line continuations, normalizes whitespace). You can call them directly:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.preprocess import preprocess_hspice
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.preprocess import preprocess_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.preprocess import preprocess_vams

cleaned = preprocess_hspice(raw_text)
cleaned = preprocess_spectre(raw_text)
cleaned = preprocess_vams(raw_text)

This is useful when you need to inspect the cleaned text before parsing, or when building a custom pipeline.

items.title: Value Utilities
items.text: The value_utils module provides functions for working with SPICE-style SI-prefixed numbers.

items.title: Parsing SI Numbers
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import parse_si_number
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import SIPrefix

pv = parse_si_number("10k")
print(pv.double_value)  # 10.0
print(pv.prefix)  # SIPrefix.KILO

pv = parse_si_number("2.2u")
print(pv.double_value)  # 2.2
print(pv.prefix)  # SIPrefix.MICRO

pv = parse_si_number("100meg")
print(pv.double_value)  # 100.0
print(pv.prefix)  # SIPrefix.MEGA

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import format_si_value
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import PrefixedValue, SIPrefix

pv = PrefixedValue(double_value=100.0, prefix=SIPrefix.PICO)

items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import parse_parameter_number

# Plain numbers -> prefixed_value with no SI prefix
pv = parse_parameter_number("42")
print(pv.prefixed_value.double_value)  # 42.0

# SI-prefixed -> prefixed_value
pv = parse_parameter_number("10k")
print(pv.prefixed_value.double_value)  # 10.0
print(pv.prefixed_value.prefix.name)  # "KILO"

Or from their format-specific modules:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.writer import write_spectre

items.title: parse_hspice(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse HSPICE netlist text. Handles .subckt/.ends, .macro/.eom, device instances, .model statements, simulation directives (.tran, .ac, .dc, .op, .fft, etc.), .include, .lib, .param.

items.title: write_hspice(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to HSPICE format.

items.title: parse_spice(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse generic SPICE netlist text. Supports the common SPICE3 subset shared across simulators.

items.title: write_spice(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to generic SPICE format.

items.title: parse_xyce(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse Xyce netlist text. Supports Xyce-specific syntax extensions.

items.title: write_xyce(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to Xyce format.

items.title: parse_spectre(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse Spectre netlist text. Handles subckt/ends, instances with (port list) circuit_name param=value syntax, model statements, and simulation analyses.

items.title: write_spectre(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to Spectre format.

items.title: parse_spectre_spice(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse Spectre-SPICE mixed-mode netlists. Handles both Spectre and SPICE syntax blocks.

items.title: write_spectre_spice(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to Spectre-SPICE format (SPICE-style output).

items.title: parse_vams(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse Verilog-AMS netlist text. Handles module/endmodule, named port connections (.port(net)), parameter overrides (#(.param(value))), natures, and disciplines.

items.title: write_vams(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist to Verilog-AMS format.

items.title: parse_systemverilog(text: str) -> Netlist
items.text: Parse the structural subset of SystemVerilog (3.1a, Annex A): ANSI and non-ANSI ports, parameter/localparam, net declarations, module instances with named, positional, .name, .* and empty connections, and assign/alias net merges. Behavioral code (always, initial, function, task, generate, ...) is kept as text in behavioral_block_N circuit properties.

items.title: write_systemverilog(circuit: Netlist) -> str
items.text: Write a Netlist as structural SystemVerilog with ANSI headers and named connections. Values are written as plain numbers (SystemVerilog has no SI suffixes).

items.title: Parsing Netlists
items.text:
Every parser takes a str of netlist text and returns a Netlist model. Here is the same RC lowpass filter parsed from each supported format:

Spectre 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre

netlist = parse_spectre("""\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
""")
HSPICE 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser import parse_hspice

netlist = parse_hspice("""\
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
""")
SPICE 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spice.parser import parse_spice

netlist = parse_spice("""\
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
""")
Xyce 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.xyce.parser import parse_xyce

netlist = parse_xyce("""\
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
""")
Verilog-AMS 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.parser import parse_vams

netlist = parse_vams("""\
module rc_lowpass (in_, out, gnd);
  inout in_, out, gnd;
  resistor #(.value(1k)) R1 (.p(in_), .n(out));
  capacitor #(.value(100p)) C1 (.p(out), .n(gnd));
endmodule
""")
Spectre-SPICE 
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre_spice.parser import parse_spectre_spice

netlist = parse_spectre_spice("""\
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
""")

All of these produce the same Netlist object with one circuit, two subcircuit instances of external circuits (resistor, capacitor), and the corresponding connections.

items.title: Writing Netlists
items.text:
Every writer takes a Netlist model and returns formatted netlist text:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.writer import write_vams
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.writer import write_hspice
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.xyce.writer import write_xyce

netlist = parse_spectre("""\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
""")

# Convert to any supported format
print(write_vams(netlist))
print(write_hspice(netlist))
print(write_xyce(netlist))

items.title: Format Conversion
items.text: The core pattern is simple: parse with one format, write with another.

items.title: Spectre to Verilog-AMS
items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.vams.writer import write_vams

spectre_text = """\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
"""

netlist = parse_spectre(spectre_text)
print(write_vams(netlist))

module rc_lowpass (in_, out, gnd);
  inout in_, out, gnd;
  resistor #(.value(1k)) R1 (.p(in_), .n(out));
  capacitor #(.value(100p)) C1 (.p(out), .n(gnd));
endmodule

vams_text = """\

  inout in_, out, vdd, vss;
  mosfet #(.L(0.18u), .W(1u)) M1 (.d(out), .g(in_), .s(vdd), .b(vdd));
  mosfet #(.L(0.18u), .W(0.5u)) M2 (.d(out), .g(in_), .s(vss), .b(vss));
endmodule
"""

netlist = parse_vams(vams_text)

items.title: From and to kfnetlist Netlists
items.text:
Two classes share the name Netlist:

  • kfnetlist.morphnet.Netlist is a schema document: circuit definitions, their subcircuit instances, external devices and simulation data.
  • kfnetlist.Netlist is the connectivity graph of one cell (instances, nets, ports) that kfnetlist uses for LVS, open detection and flattening.

Both follow the kfnetlist schema (circuit.proto), so two functions bridge them. morphnet.from_netlists() turns {cell name: kfnetlist.Netlist} into a morphnet Netlist ready for any writer, and morphnet.to_netlists() turns any parsed or built morphnet Netlist into one kfnetlist.Netlist per circuit:

from kfnetlist import Netlist, NetlistPort, PortRef, morphnet
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist import parse_spectre, write_spectre

nl = Netlist()
nl.create_inst("R1", kcl="", component="resistor", settings={"value": 1000.0})
nl.create_inst("C1", kcl="", component="capacitor", settings={"value": 1e-10})
for port in ("vin", "vout", "gnd"):
    nl.create_port(port)
nl.create_net(NetlistPort("vin"), PortRef("R1", "p"))
nl.create_net(PortRef("R1", "n"), PortRef("C1", "p"), NetlistPort("vout"))
nl.create_net(PortRef("C1", "n"), NetlistPort("gnd"))

netlist = morphnet.from_netlists({"rc": nl}, toplevel="rc")
print(write_spectre(netlist))

netlists = morphnet.to_netlists(parse_spectre(write_spectre(netlist)))

Output:

subckt rc (vin gnd vout)
R1 (vin vout) resistor value=1000
C1 (vout gnd) capacitor value=1e-10
ends rc

Things to know:

  • Pin order. Built-in devices (resistor, capacitor, inductor, diode, bjt, mosfet, vsource, isource) get the same pin order the SPICE parser uses. For other components, add an ext_circuit(..., ports=[...]) to the netlist so positional formats (SPICE, Spectre) know their pin order.
  • Net names. A net that contains a top-level port is named after the port. Other nets are named net_<i>, because kfnetlist's document model does not carry net names yet.
  • Values. SI prefixes are applied (1k becomes 1000.0). Non-numeric parameters (model references) are not converted to kfnetlist.Netlist settings, and directives, libraries and simulation data stay on the morphnet Netlist.
  • Names. Instance names are written as-is. SPICE infers the device type from the first letter, so use SPICE prefixes (R1, C1, X... for subcircuit calls) when SPICE output matters.
  • Standalone package. The vendored schema registers circuit.proto in protobuf's global pool, as the standalone mphnet package does. Don't import both in the same process.

items.text:
from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser import parse_hspice

items.title: Extending kfnetlist.morphnet with New Formats
items.text: kfnetlist.morphnet follows a consistent 5-module pattern for every netlist format. To add support for a new format (e.g., myformat), create the following modules under src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/
  __init__.py          # empty
  preprocess.py        # text normalization
  transformer.py       # parse tree -> Netlist
  parser.py            # grammar + orchestration
  writer.py            # Netlist -> text

Plus a grammar file:

src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/grammars/myformat.lark

items.title: Step 1: Write the Lark Grammar
items.text:
Create src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/grammars/myformat.lark.

kfnetlist.morphnet grammars use Lark EBNF syntax. The LALR parser is preferred for performance; use Earley only if the grammar is inherently ambiguous.

// myformat.lark
start: toplevel_item*

?toplevel_item: subckt_def
              | instance_stmt

subckt_def: "SUBCKT" IDENT port_decl+ body "END"
// ... define terminals and rules for your format

Every grammar must define a start rule that produces the top-level netlist structure.

Shared terminals (identifiers, SI numbers) can be imported from common.lark:

%import .common.IDENT
%import .common.SI_NUMBER

Tip

Start from an existing grammar as a reference. spectre.lark and spice.lark in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/grammars/ are good starting points.

items.title: Step 2: Create the Preprocessor
items.text:
Create src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/preprocess.py to normalize raw input before parsing. Most formats need comment stripping, line continuation joining, or whitespace normalization:

# src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/preprocess.py


def preprocess_myformat(text: str) -> str:
    # Strip comments, join continuations, normalize whitespace
    ...
    return cleaned

items.title: Step 3: Implement the Transformer
items.text:
Create src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/transformer.py with a Lark Transformer subclass that converts the parse tree into a Netlist model:

# src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/transformer.py
from __future__ import annotations

from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist, Circuit, Port, SubCircuit, Connection
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.net_utils import NetMap, add_port_to_net, net_map_to_connections
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import parse_si_number


class MyFormatTransformer(Transformer):
    def subckt_def(self, items):
        # Build a Circuit from the parsed subcircuit
        ...

        ...

    def start(self, items):

        return Netlist(circuits=..., ext_circuits=...)

The transformer must produce a valid Netlist object — the same protobuf-backed Pydantic model that all other formats use.

Reuse utilities

Use net_map_to_connections from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.net_utils to convert net-based connectivity (common in SPICE) to point-to-point Connection objects. Use parse_si_number from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils to parse SI-prefixed parameter values.

items.title: Step 4: Implement the Parser
items.text:
Create src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/parser.py following the established pattern: a class with a cached Lark instance, a parse() classmethod, and a module-level convenience function:

# src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/parser.py
from __future__ import annotations

from importlib.resources import files as resource_files
from typing import ClassVar

from lark import Lark

from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.myformat.preprocess import preprocess_myformat
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.myformat.transformer import MyFormatTransformer


class MyFormatParser:
    lark_instance: ClassVar[Lark | None] = None

    @classmethod
    def get_lark(cls) -> Lark:
        if cls.lark_instance is None:
            grammar_text = (
                resource_files("kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.grammars")
                .joinpath("myformat.lark")
                .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            )
            cls.lark_instance = Lark(grammar_text, parser="lalr")
        return cls.lark_instance

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Netlist:
        cleaned = preprocess_myformat(text)
        tree = cls.get_lark().parse(cleaned)
        return MyFormatTransformer().transform(tree)


def parse_myformat(text: str) -> Netlist:
    return MyFormatParser.parse(text)

items.title: Step 5: Implement the Writer
items.text:
Create src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/writer.py that takes a Netlist and produces formatted netlist text:

# src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/myformat/writer.py
from __future__ import annotations

from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.net_utils import connections_to_instance_nets
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import format_si_value


class MyFormatWriter:
    def write(self, netlist: Netlist) -> str:
        lines = []
        for circuit in netlist.circuits:
            # Emit subcircuit header
            # Emit instances with port connections and parameters
            # Emit footer
            ...
        return "\n".join(lines)


def write_myformat(netlist: Netlist) -> str:
    return MyFormatWriter().write(netlist)

Reuse utilities

Use connections_to_instance_nets to build a (instance_name, port_name) -> net_name lookup from the module's connections. Use format_si_value to emit SI-prefixed parameter values.

items.title: Protobuf Schema Changes
items.text:
If you need to modify the circuit or simulation protobuf schemas:

  1. Edit the .proto files in crates/kfnetlist-schema/proto/ (the single schema source shared with the Rust core)
  2. Run just compile-schema-py to regenerate the Python bindings, and update crates/kfnetlist-schema/src/convert.rs if the netlist mapping changes
  3. Update the corresponding Pydantic models in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/morphnet_schema/
  4. Run the full test suite to verify nothing broke

items.title: Coding Standards
items.text:
This project follows PEP 8 enforced by Ruff:

  • Line length: 88 characters (Ruff default)
  • Formatting: just format (runs ruff format)
  • Linting: just lint (runs ruff check)
  • Naming: snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants
  • Type annotations: Required on all public function signatures
  • Testing: pytest with parametrized tests for multi-format coverage
  • No inline comments unless explaining a non-obvious constraint

items.title: Converting between formats
items.text: Download notebook (.ipynb)

items.title: Converting between formats
items.text:
Every format has a parser into the morphnet Netlist and a writer out of it, so converting a netlist is one line: parse with one format, write with another. This page:

  1. walks through conversions between pairs of formats, with full output;
  2. converts one circuit through all 7 × 7 format pairs and checks that connectivity and parameters survive;
  3. round-trips a photonic MZI through every format, checking that its waveguide nets stay waveguide;
  4. goes from a kfnetlist.Netlist to every format and back.

The example netlists of each format are described on Parsing netlist formats.

from kfnetlist import Netlist, NetlistPort, PortRef, morphnet
from kfnetlist.morphnet import netlist as formats

FORMATS = [
    "spice",
    "hspice",
    "xyce",
    "spectre",
    "spectre_spice",
    "vams",
    "systemverilog",
]


def convert(text: str, src: str, dst: str) -> str:
    """Convert netlist text from format `src` to format `dst`."""
    parse = getattr(formats, f"parse_{src}")
    write = getattr(formats, f"write_{dst}")
    return write(parse(text))

The same helper is a ten-line command-line converter (docs/assets/convert_demo.py): python convert_demo.py spice spectre < in.sp.

items.title: SPICE → Spectre
items.text:
SPICE primitives (M, R, C, ...) become Spectre instances of the model or primitive; subcircuit calls keep their pin order.

SPICE = """\
* CMOS buffer
.subckt inverter in out vdd vss
M1 out in vdd vdd pch W=2u L=180n
M2 out in vss vss nch W=1u L=180n
.ends inverter
.subckt buffer a y vdd vss
X1 a mid vdd vss inverter
X2 mid y vdd vss inverter
C1 y vss 10f
.ends buffer
.end
"""
print(convert(SPICE, "spice", "spectre"))

subckt inverter (in out vdd vss)
M1 (out in vdd vdd) pch W=2u L=180n
M2 (out in vss vss) nch W=1u L=180n
ends inverter
subckt buffer (a y vdd vss)
X1 (a mid vdd vss) inverter
X2 (mid y vdd vss) inverter
C1 (y vss) capacitor value=10f
ends buffer

items.title: Spectre → Verilog-AMS
items.text:
Positional Spectre terminals become named Verilog connections, using the pin names of the subcircuit or primitive (d, g, s, b for a MOSFET).

SPECTRE = """\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor r=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor c=100p
ends rc_lowpass
"""
print(convert(SPECTRE, "spectre", "vams"))

module rc_lowpass (in_, out, gnd);
  inout in_, out, gnd;
  resistor #(.r(1k)) R1 (.p(in_), .n(out));
  capacitor #(.c(100p)) C1 (.p(out), .n(gnd));
endmodule

items.title: Verilog-AMS → SystemVerilog
items.text:
SystemVerilog has no SI suffixes, so 10k is written as 10000. The Verilog-AMS discipline (electrical) is kept as the port's net type.

VAMS = """\
module divider (vin, vout, gnd);
  input vin;
  output vout;
  inout gnd;
  electrical vin, vout, gnd;
  resistor #(.r(10k)) R1 (.p(vin), .n(vout));
  resistor #(.r(10k)) R2 (.p(vout), .n(gnd));
endmodule
"""
print(convert(VAMS, "vams", "systemverilog"))

module divider (
  input electrical vin,
  output electrical vout,
  inout electrical gnd
);
  resistor #(.r(10000)) R1 (.p(vin), .n(vout));
  resistor #(.r(10000)) R2 (.p(vout), .n(gnd));
endmodule

items.title: SystemVerilog → SPICE
items.text:
Named connections are put back in definition order: modules defined in the same file become .subckt blocks and built-in devices (mosfet, resistor, ...) become SPICE primitives with their fixed pin order. Behavioral code (always, assign with logic) is not structure and is not written to SPICE.

SPICE picks the element type from the first letter of the instance name, so subcircuit instances must be named X... and devices M..., R..., ... for the SPICE output to parse back.

SYSTEMVERILOG = """\
module inv (input a, output y, inout vdd, vss);
  mosfet #(.W(2e-6), .L(180e-9)) MP (.d(y), .g(a), .s(vdd), .b(vdd));
  mosfet #(.W(1e-6), .L(180e-9)) MN (.d(y), .g(a), .s(vss), .b(vss));
endmodule
module ring3 (output osc, inout vdd, vss);
  inv X1 (.a(osc), .y(n1), .*);
  inv X2 (.a(n1), .y(n2), .*);
  inv X3 (.a(n2), .y(osc), .*);
  always @(posedge osc) $display("tick");
endmodule
"""
print(convert(SYSTEMVERILOG, "systemverilog", "spice"))

* untitled
.subckt inv a y vdd vss
MP y a vdd vdd W=2e-06 L=1.8e-07
MN y a vss vss W=1e-06 L=1.8e-07
.ends inv
.subckt ring3 osc vdd vss
X1 osc n1 vdd vss inv
X2 n1 n2 vdd vss inv
X3 n2 osc vdd vss inv
.ends ring3
.end

items.title: HSPICE → Xyce
items.text:
HSPICE = """\
* RC low-pass
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k     $ series resistor
C1 out gnd 100p   $ shunt capacitor
.ends rc_lowpass
.end
"""
print(convert(HSPICE, "hspice", "xyce"))

* untitled
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
.end

items.title: Mixed Spectre / SPICE → SystemVerilog
items.text:
A deck that switches language with simulator lang=... comes out as one SystemVerilog file:

SPECTRE_SPICE = """\
simulator lang=spice
.subckt rdiv a b mid
R1 a mid 1k
R2 mid b 1k
.ends rdiv
simulator lang=spectre
subckt top (vin gnd)
X0 (vin gnd tap) rdiv
C0 (tap gnd) capacitor c=1p
ends top
"""
print(convert(SPECTRE_SPICE, "spectre_spice", "systemverilog"))

module rdiv (
  inout a,
  inout b,
  inout mid
);
  resistor #(.value(1000)) R1 (.p(a), .n(mid));
  resistor #(.value(1000)) R2 (.p(mid), .n(b));
endmodule

module top (
  inout vin,
  inout gnd
);
  rdiv X0 (.a(vin), .b(gnd), .mid(tap));
  capacitor #(.c(1e-12)) C0 (.p(tap), .n(gnd));
endmodule

The same CMOS buffer, written by hand in each of the 7 formats:

  electrical in, out, vdd, vss;

endmodule

""",

endmodule
module buffer (inout a, y, vdd, vss);
  inverter X1 (.in(a), .out(mid), .vdd, .vss);

endmodule

Two netlists are "the same" when every circuit has the same ports, the same nets and the same instances with the same component and settings, as seen by kfnetlist.Netlist:

def graph(netlist: morphnet.Netlist) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for name, nl in morphnet.to_netlists(netlist).items():
        nl.sort()
        nets = sorted(
            sorted(
                m.name if isinstance(m, NetlistPort) else f"{m.instance}.{m.port}"
                for m in net
            )
            for net in nl.nets
        )
        instances = {
            k: (v.component, {s: float(f"{x:.9g}") for s, x in v.settings.items()})
            for k, v in nl.instances.items()
        }
        out[name] = (sorted(p.name for p in nl.ports), nets, instances)
    return out


reference = graph(formats.parse_spice(SPICE))
for name, (ports, nets, instances) in reference.items():
    print(f"{name}: ports={ports}")
    print(f"  nets={nets}")
    print(f"  instances={instances}")

inverter: ports=['in', 'out', 'vdd', 'vss']
  nets=[['M1.b', 'M1.s', 'vdd'], ['M1.d', 'M2.d', 'out'], ['M1.g', 'M2.g', 'in'], ['M2.b', 'M2.s', 'vss']]
  instances={'M1': ('mosfet', {'L': 1.8e-07, 'W': 2e-06}), 'M2': ('mosfet', {'L': 1.8e-07, 'W': 1e-06})}
buffer: ports=['a', 'vdd', 'vss', 'y']
  nets=[['C1.n', 'X1.vss', 'X2.vss', 'vss'], ['C1.p', 'X2.out', 'y'], ['X1.in', 'a'], ['X1.out', 'X2.in'], ['X1.vdd', 'X2.vdd', 'vdd']]
  instances={'C1': ('capacitor', {'value': 1e-14}), 'X1': ('inverter', {}), 'X2': ('inverter', {})}

    parsed = getattr(formats, f"parse_{src}")(text)
    print(f"{src:>14}: {'same' if graph(parsed) == reference else 'DIFFERENT'}")

items.title: A photonic MZI through every format
items.text:
Terminals named o1, o2, ... are waveguide terminals in every format, so a photonic circuit keeps its waveguide nets through any conversion. The leaf cells are declared as empty modules so that every format knows their pin names:

MZI = """\
module dc #(parameter real gap = 200e-9) (inout o1, o2, o3, o4);
endmodule
module wg #(parameter real length = 100e-6) (inout o1, o2);
endmodule
module heater_wg #(parameter real length = 100e-6) (inout o1, o2, e1, e2);
endmodule

module mzi (input o1, o2, output o3, o4, input e1, inout gnd);
  dc #(.gap(200e-9)) Xdc1 (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(top_a), .o4(bot_a));
  dc #(.gap(200e-9)) Xdc2 (.o1(top_b), .o2(bot_b), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
  heater_wg Xtop (.o1(top_a), .o2(top_b), .e1(e1), .e2(gnd));
  wg Xbot (.o1(bot_a), .o2(bot_b));
endmodule
"""
mzi = formats.parse_systemverilog(MZI)


def net_domains(netlist: morphnet.Netlist) -> dict[str, str]:
    top = next(c for c in netlist.circuits if c.name == "mzi")
    return {c.name: c.domain.name.lower() for c in top.connections}


expected = net_domains(mzi)
print(expected)

{'o1': 'waveguide', 'o2': 'waveguide', 'o3': 'waveguide', 'o4': 'waveguide', 'e1': 'electrical', 'gnd': 'electrical', 'top_a': 'waveguide', 'bot_a': 'waveguide', 'top_b': 'waveguide', 'bot_b': 'waveguide'}

for dst in FORMATS:
    text = getattr(formats, f"write_{dst}")(mzi)
    back = getattr(formats, f"parse_{dst}")(text)
    assert net_domains(back) == expected, dst
    assert graph(back) == graph(mzi), dst
    print(
        f"{dst:>14}: waveguide nets {sorted(n for n, d in expected.items() if d == 'waveguide')}"
    )

         spice: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']
        hspice: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']
          xyce: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']
       spectre: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']
 spectre_spice: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']
          vams: waveguide nets ['bot_a', 'bot_b', 'o1', 'o2', 'o3', 'o4', 'top_a', 'top_b']

  parameter real gap = 2e-07;
endmodule

  parameter real length = 0.0001;
endmodule

  parameter real length = 0.0001;
endmodule
module mzi (o1, o2, o3, o4, e1, gnd);
  input o1, o2, e1;
  output o3, o4;
  inout gnd;
  dc #(.gap(2e-07)) Xdc1 (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(top_a), .o4(bot_a));
  dc #(.gap(2e-07)) Xdc2 (.o1(top_b), .o2(bot_b), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
  heater_wg Xtop (.o1(top_a), .o2(top_b), .e1(e1), .e2(gnd));
  wg Xbot (.o1(bot_a), .o2(bot_b));
endmodule

items.title: From kfnetlist.Netlist to any format and back
items.text:
morphnet.from_netlists() turns {cell name: kfnetlist.Netlist} into a morphnet Netlist. Instances of built-in devices (resistor, capacitor, mosfet, ...) get the same pin declarations the SPICE parser creates, so positional formats write their pins in device order.

rc = Netlist()
rc.create_inst("R1", kcl="", component="resistor", settings={"value": 1000.0})
rc.create_inst("C1", kcl="", component="capacitor", settings={"value": 1e-10})
for port in ("vin", "vout", "gnd"):
    rc.create_port(port)
rc.create_net(NetlistPort("vin"), PortRef("R1", "p"))
rc.create_net(PortRef("R1", "n"), PortRef("C1", "p"), NetlistPort("vout"))
rc.create_net(PortRef("C1", "n"), NetlistPort("gnd"))
rc.sort()

doc = morphnet.from_netlists({"rc": rc}, "rc")
for dst in FORMATS:
    text = getattr(formats, f"write_{dst}")(doc)
    back = getattr(formats, f"parse_{dst}")(text)
    print(f"{dst:>14}: {'same graph' if graph(back) == graph(doc) else 'DIFFERENT'}")

         spice: same graph


        hspice: same graph
          xyce: same graph
       spectre: same graph
 spectre_spice: same graph
          vams: same graph
 systemverilog: same graph

Ports, nets, components and settings come back unchanged. kfnetlist-only instance data (instance arrays, placement) has no place in the text formats; use to_json() / protobuf for a lossless copy.

print(formats.write_systemverilog(doc))

module rc (
  inout gnd,
  inout vin,
  inout vout
);
  capacitor #(.value(1e-10)) C1 (.p(vout), .n(gnd));
  resistor #(.value(1000)) R1 (.p(vin), .n(vout));
endmodule

items.title: Your First Parse
items.text:
Parse a Spectre netlist into kfnetlist.morphnet's intermediate representation:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre

text = """\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
"""

netlist = parse_spectre(text)

print(netlist.top_circuit)  # "rc_lowpass"
print(len(netlist.circuits))  # 1

The netlist object is a Netlist model — kfnetlist.morphnet's common intermediate representation. Every parser produces the same type, regardless of the input format.

items.title: Your First Conversion
items.text:
Convert from one format to another by combining a parser with a writer:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.spectre.parser import parse_spectre
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.writer import write_hspice

spectre_text = """\
subckt rc_lowpass (in_ out gnd)
R1 (in_ out) resistor value=1k
C1 (out gnd) capacitor value=100p
ends rc_lowpass
"""

netlist = parse_spectre(spectre_text)
hspice_text = write_hspice(netlist)
print(hspice_text)

Output:

.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass

items.title: YAML Roundtrip
items.text:
Every Netlist object can be serialized to and from YAML for portable interchange:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.morphnet_schema import Netlist
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.hspice.parser import parse_hspice

netlist = parse_hspice("""\
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k
C1 out gnd 100p
.ends rc_lowpass
""")

yaml_str = netlist.to_yaml()
restored = Netlist.from_yaml(yaml_str)

assert restored == netlist

items.title: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export
items.text:
A Mach-Zehnder interferometer built hierarchically with the kfnetlist.morphnet builder API. The notebook then:

  1. converts it to kfnetlist.Netlist graphs,
  2. flattens the coupler sub-cells with kfnetlist,
  3. exports the flat netlist to Verilog-AMS, Spectre and SPICE.

Adapted from morphnet's examples/mzi.py. The changes:

  • Each delay arm now sits between the couplers (o1, then o2); the original wired the arm input and the next coupler to the same net.
  • Optical terminals follow the gdsfactory naming o1, o2, ... (inputs first), which every netlist parser reads as waveguide terminals.
  • The external circuits declare their ports.
  • Nets that reach a circuit terminal are named after it.
  • Instance names start with X, SPICE's prefix for subcircuit calls, so the SPICE export is valid.
from kfnetlist import morphnet
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist import write_spectre, write_spice, write_vams

WG = morphnet.SignalDomain.WAVEGUIDE
IN, OUT = morphnet.PortDirection.INPUT, morphnet.PortDirection.OUTPUT
path: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export

items.title: Directional coupler sub-cell
items.text:
Parameter defaults are given as (name, value) tuples. The terminals are in the waveguide domain.

dc = morphnet.circuit("dc_coupler", parameters=[("gap", 200e-9), ("length", 10e-6)])
for name in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"):
    dc.add_terminal(name, direction=IN if name in ("o1", "o2") else OUT, domain=WG)

dc.add(morphnet.subcircuit("Xcoupler", "wg_directional_coupler"))
for name in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"):
    dc.connect(name, ("", name), ("Xcoupler", name), domain=WG)
path: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export

items.title: MZI top cell
items.text:
Two couplers, with a delay arm on each path between them.

mzi = morphnet.circuit("mzi", parameters=[("arm_length", 100e-6)])
for name in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"):
    mzi.add_terminal(name, direction=IN if name in ("o1", "o2") else OUT, domain=WG)

mzi.add(
    morphnet.subcircuit("Xdc1", "dc_coupler"),
    morphnet.subcircuit("Xdc2", "dc_coupler"),
    morphnet.subcircuit("Xarm_top", "wg_delay"),
    morphnet.subcircuit("Xarm_bot", "wg_delay"),
)
for net, *ends in [
    ("o1", ("", "o1"), ("Xdc1", "o1")),
    ("o2", ("", "o2"), ("Xdc1", "o2")),
    ("top_a", ("Xdc1", "o3"), ("Xarm_top", "o1")),
    ("top_b", ("Xarm_top", "o2"), ("Xdc2", "o1")),
    ("bot_a", ("Xdc1", "o4"), ("Xarm_bot", "o1")),
    ("bot_b", ("Xarm_bot", "o2"), ("Xdc2", "o2")),
    ("o3", ("Xdc2", "o3"), ("", "o3")),
    ("o4", ("Xdc2", "o4"), ("", "o4")),
]:
    mzi.connect(net, *ends, domain=WG)
path: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export

items.title: Netlist with a photonic PDK library
items.text:
ckt = morphnet.Netlist(name="mzi_chip", top_circuit="mzi")
ckt.add_library(
    "photonic_pdk",
    morphnet.external_library(
        "path/to/photonic_pdk.lib",
        model_type="photonic",
        external_model_names=["wg_directional_coupler", "wg_delay"],
    ),
)
ckt.add_ext(
    morphnet.ext_circuit(
        "wg_directional_coupler",
        class_name="dc",
        library_name="photonic_pdk",
        ports=[morphnet.port(p, domain=WG) for p in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4")],
    ),
    morphnet.ext_circuit(
        "wg_delay",
        class_name="delay_line",
        library_name="photonic_pdk",
        ports=[morphnet.port(p, domain=WG) for p in ("o1", "o2")],
    ),
)
ckt.add(mzi, dc)

mzi_module = next(m for m in ckt.circuits if m.name == "mzi")
assert all(t.domain == WG for t in mzi_module.ports)
print(write_vams(ckt))

module mzi (o1, o2, o3, o4);
  input o1, o2;
  output o3, o4;
  parameter arm_length = 0.0001;
  dc_coupler Xdc1 (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(top_a), .o4(bot_a));
  dc_coupler Xdc2 (.o1(top_b), .o2(bot_b), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
  wg_delay Xarm_top (.o1(top_a), .o2(top_b));
  wg_delay Xarm_bot (.o1(bot_a), .o2(bot_b));
endmodule
module dc_coupler (o1, o2, o3, o4);
  input o1, o2;
  output o3, o4;
  parameter gap = 2e-07;
  parameter length = 1e-05;
  wg_directional_coupler Xcoupler (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
endmodule
path: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export

items.title: Into kfnetlist
items.text:
to_netlists gives one kfnetlist.Netlist per circuit, so all of kfnetlist's tooling applies: open detection, LVS diffs, flattening.

netlists = morphnet.to_netlists(ckt)
print({name: nl for name, nl in netlists.items()})
print("opens:", netlists["mzi"].detect_opens())

{'mzi': Netlist(instances=4, nets=8, ports=4), 'dc_coupler': Netlist(instances=1, nets=4, ports=4)}
opens: {'unconnected_ports': [], 'singleton_nets': []}

Flatten the two coupler instances into their contents:

flat = netlists["mzi"].flatten(
    netlists,
    instance_cell_map={"Xdc1": "dc_coupler", "Xdc2": "dc_coupler"},
    separator="_",  # keeps flattened names valid identifiers in every format
)
flat.sort()
print("instances:", flat.instance_names())

instances: ['Xarm_bot', 'Xarm_top', 'Xdc1_Xcoupler', 'Xdc2_Xcoupler']
path: Photonic MZI: builder API, kfnetlist round trip, export

items.title: And back out, in any format
items.text:
from_netlists turns the flat kfnetlist.Netlist back into a morphnet Netlist. The external circuits are declared again so the positional formats keep the pin order.

flat_ckt = morphnet.from_netlists({"mzi_flat": flat}, "mzi_flat")
flat_ckt.add_ext(*ckt.ext_circuits)
print(write_vams(flat_ckt))
print(write_spectre(flat_ckt))
print(write_spice(flat_ckt))

module mzi_flat (o1, o2, o3, o4);
  inout o1, o2, o3, o4;
  wg_delay Xarm_bot (.o1(net_4), .o2(net_5));
  wg_delay Xarm_top (.o1(net_6), .o2(net_7));
  wg_directional_coupler Xdc1_Xcoupler (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(net_6), .o4(net_4));
  wg_directional_coupler Xdc2_Xcoupler (.o1(net_7), .o2(net_5), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
endmodule

subckt mzi_flat (o1 o2 o3 o4)
Xarm_bot (net_4 net_5) wg_delay
Xarm_top (net_6 net_7) wg_delay
Xdc1_Xcoupler (o1 o2 net_6 net_4) wg_directional_coupler
Xdc2_Xcoupler (net_7 net_5 o3 o4) wg_directional_coupler
ends mzi_flat

* mzi_flat
.subckt mzi_flat o1 o2 o3 o4
Xarm_bot net_4 net_5 wg_delay
Xarm_top net_6 net_7 wg_delay
Xdc1_Xcoupler o1 o2 net_6 net_4 wg_directional_coupler
Xdc2_Xcoupler net_7 net_5 o3 o4 wg_directional_coupler
.ends mzi_flat
.end
