items.title: Parsing netlist formats
items.text: Download notebook (.ipynb)

items.title: Parsing netlist formats
items.text:
kfnetlist.morphnet reads seven netlist formats into one schema document, the morphnet Netlist (circuits, subcircuit instances, connections, parameters, directives). morphnet.to_netlists() then turns every circuit into a kfnetlist.Netlist connectivity graph.

Format Parser Writer Typical extension SPICE (ngspice / generic) parse_spice write_spice .sp, .cir HSPICE parse_hspice write_hspice .sp Xyce parse_xyce write_xyce .cir Spectre parse_spectre write_spectre .scs Spectre with simulator lang=spice blocks parse_spectre_spice write_spectre_spice .scs Verilog-AMS parse_vams write_vams .vams, .va SystemVerilog (structural) parse_systemverilog write_systemverilog .sv

This page defines one example netlist per format, parses it, and shows what ends up in the morphnet Netlist and in kfnetlist.Netlist. The conversion page writes them back out in other formats.

Waveguide or electrical? Every parser applies the same rule to terminal names: o1, o2, ... are waveguide (optical) terminals, while e1, e2, ... and names without a prefix are electrical. A net that touches an o<N> terminal is a waveguide net.

from collections import defaultdict

from kfnetlist import NetlistPort, morphnet
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist import (
    parse_hspice,
    parse_spectre,
    parse_spectre_spice,
    parse_spice,
    parse_systemverilog,
    parse_vams,
    parse_xyce,
)
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.value_utils import format_si_value


def value(param: morphnet.Parameter) -> str:
    pv = param.default_value
    if pv is not None and pv.prefixed_value is not None:
        return format_si_value(pv.prefixed_value)
    return param.properties.get("expr", "?")


def summary(netlist: morphnet.Netlist) -> None:
    """Print what a parser put into a morphnet Netlist."""
    print("top circuit:", netlist.top_circuit)
    for d in netlist.directives:
        print("directive:", d.kind.name, " ".join(filter(None, (d.name, d.value))))
    for ext in netlist.ext_circuits:
        ports = ", ".join(p.name for p in ext.ports)
        print(f"external circuit: {ext.name}({ports}) {ext.properties}")
    for c in netlist.circuits:
        print(f"\ncircuit {c.name}")
        if c.parameters:
            print(
                "  parameters:", ", ".join(f"{p.name}={value(p)}" for p in c.parameters)
            )
        print(
            "  ports:",
            ", ".join(
                f"{p.name} ({p.direction.name.lower()}, {p.domain.name.lower()})"
                for p in c.ports
            ),
        )
        for s in c.subcircuits:
            params = " ".join(f"{p.name}={value(p)}" for p in s.parameters)
            model = s.properties.get("model_name", "")
            print(f"  instance {s.name}: {s.circuit_name} {model} {params}".rstrip())
        nets: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
        domains = {}
        for conn in c.connections:
            for ref in (conn.source, conn.target):
                if ref is None:
                    continue
                pin = (
                    f"{ref.instance_name}.{ref.port_name}"
                    if ref.instance_name
                    else ref.port_name
                )
                if pin not in nets[conn.name]:
                    nets[conn.name].append(pin)
            domains[conn.name] = conn.domain.name.lower()
        for name, pins in nets.items():
            print(f"  net {name} [{domains[name]}]: {', '.join(pins)}")
        for key, text in c.properties.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {' '.join(text.split())}")


def show_kfnetlist(netlist: morphnet.Netlist, cell: str) -> None:
    """Print the kfnetlist.Netlist that morphnet.to_netlists() builds for `cell`."""
    nl = morphnet.to_netlists(netlist)[cell]
    nl.sort()
    print("ports:", [p.name for p in nl.ports])
    for name, inst in nl.instances.items():
        print(f"instance {name}: component={inst.component!r} settings={inst.settings}")
    for net in nl.nets:
        print(
            "net:",
            " -- ".join(
                m.name if isinstance(m, NetlistPort) else f"{m.instance}.{m.port}"
                for m in net
            ),
        )

items.title: SPICE
items.text:
A generic SPICE deck: device models, a CMOS inverter subcircuit, and a buffer built from two inverters. Primitive devices (R, C, L, D, Q, M, V, I) become instances of external circuits (resistor, mosfet, ...) with fixed pin names (p/n, d/g/s/b, ...). The model name is kept in the instance's model_name property.

SPICE = """\
* CMOS buffer
.model nch nmos level=49 vth0=0.4
.model pch pmos level=49 vth0=-0.4

.subckt inverter in out vdd vss
M1 out in vdd vdd pch W=2u L=180n
M2 out in vss vss nch W=1u L=180n
.ends inverter

.subckt buffer a y vdd vss
X1 a mid vdd vss inverter
X2 mid y vdd vss inverter
C1 y vss 10f
.ends buffer
.end
"""
spice = parse_spice(SPICE)
summary(spice)

top circuit: buffer
external circuit: mosfet(d, g, s, b) {'spice_prefix': 'M'}
external circuit: capacitor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'C'}
external circuit: nch() {'model_type': 'nmos'}
external circuit: pch() {'model_type': 'pmos'}

circuit inverter
  ports: in (inout, electrical), out (inout, electrical), vdd (inout, electrical), vss (inout, electrical)
  instance M1: mosfet pch W=2u L=180n
  instance M2: mosfet nch W=1u L=180n
  net in [electrical]: in, M1.g, M2.g
  net out [electrical]: out, M1.d, M2.d
  net vdd [electrical]: vdd, M1.s, M1.b
  net vss [electrical]: vss, M2.s, M2.b

circuit buffer
  ports: a (inout, electrical), y (inout, electrical), vdd (inout, electrical), vss (inout, electrical)
  instance X1: inverter
  instance X2: inverter
  instance C1: capacitor  value=10f
  net a [electrical]: a, X1.in
  net y [electrical]: y, X2.out, C1.p
  net vdd [electrical]: vdd, X1.vdd, X2.vdd
  net vss [electrical]: vss, X1.vss, X2.vss, C1.n
  net mid [electrical]: X1.out, X2.in

to_netlists() returns one kfnetlist.Netlist per circuit. Instances keep their parameters as settings; SI values become plain floats:

show_kfnetlist(spice, "inverter")

ports: ['in', 'out', 'vdd', 'vss']
instance M1: component='mosfet' settings={'L': 1.8000000000000002e-07, 'W': 2e-06}
instance M2: component='mosfet' settings={'L': 1.8000000000000002e-07, 'W': 1e-06}
net: in -- M1.g -- M2.g
net: out -- M1.d -- M2.d
net: vdd -- M1.b -- M1.s
net: vss -- M2.b -- M2.s

show_kfnetlist(spice, "buffer")

ports: ['a', 'vdd', 'vss', 'y']
instance C1: component='capacitor' settings={'value': 1.0000000000000002e-14}
instance X1: component='inverter' settings={}
instance X2: component='inverter' settings={}
net: a -- X1.in
net: vdd -- X1.vdd -- X2.vdd
net: vss -- C1.n -- X1.vss -- X2.vss
net: y -- C1.p -- X2.out
net: X1.out -- X2.in

items.title: HSPICE
items.text:
HSPICE is parsed with the SPICE grammar plus HSPICE preprocessing (for example, $ comments). Here is an RC low-pass filter with an HSPICE inline comment:

HSPICE = """\
* RC low-pass
.subckt rc_lowpass in_ out gnd
R1 in_ out 1k     $ series resistor
C1 out gnd 100p   $ shunt capacitor
.ends rc_lowpass
.end
"""
hspice = parse_hspice(HSPICE)
summary(hspice)

top circuit: rc_lowpass
external circuit: resistor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'R'}
external circuit: capacitor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'C'}

circuit rc_lowpass
  ports: in_ (inout, electrical), out (inout, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)
  instance R1: resistor  value=1k
  instance C1: capacitor  value=100p
  net in_ [electrical]: in_, R1.p
  net out [electrical]: out, R1.n, C1.p
  net gnd [electrical]: gnd, C1.n

show_kfnetlist(hspice, "rc_lowpass")

ports: ['gnd', 'in_', 'out']
instance C1: component='capacitor' settings={'value': 1e-10}
instance R1: component='resistor' settings={'value': 1000.0}
net: gnd -- C1.n
net: in_ -- R1.p
net: out -- C1.p -- R1.n

items.title: Xyce
items.text:
Xyce decks are case-insensitive and declare subcircuit parameters with PARAMS:. A resistive divider, where each resistor value is a subcircuit parameter:

XYCE = """\
* Xyce divider
.SUBCKT divider vin vout gnd PARAMS: rtop=10k rbot=10k
R1 vin vout 10k
R2 vout gnd 10k
.ENDS divider
.END
"""
xyce = parse_xyce(XYCE)
summary(xyce)

top circuit: divider
external circuit: resistor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'R'}

circuit divider
  parameters: rtop=10k, rbot=10k
  ports: vin (inout, electrical), vout (inout, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)
  instance R1: resistor  value=10k
  instance R2: resistor  value=10k
  net vin [electrical]: vin, R1.p
  net vout [electrical]: vout, R1.n, R2.p
  net gnd [electrical]: gnd, R2.n

show_kfnetlist(xyce, "divider")

ports: ['gnd', 'vin', 'vout']
instance R1: component='resistor' settings={'value': 10000.0}
instance R2: component='resistor' settings={'value': 10000.0}
net: gnd -- R2.n
net: vin -- R1.p
net: vout -- R1.n -- R2.p

items.title: Spectre
items.text:
Spectre puts terminals in parentheses and names the master after them. A two-stage hierarchy:

SPECTRE = """\
subckt inverter (in_ out vdd vss)
MP (out in_ vdd vdd) pch w=2u l=180n
MN (out in_ vss vss) nch w=1u l=180n
ends inverter

subckt buffer (a y vdd vss)
I1 (a mid vdd vss) inverter
I2 (mid y vdd vss) inverter
ends buffer
"""
spectre = parse_spectre(SPECTRE)
summary(spectre)

top circuit: buffer
external circuit: mosfet(d, g, s, b) {'spice_prefix': 'M'}

circuit inverter
  ports: in_ (inout, electrical), out (inout, electrical), vdd (inout, electrical), vss (inout, electrical)
  instance MP: mosfet pch w=2u l=180n
  instance MN: mosfet nch w=1u l=180n
  net in_ [electrical]: in_, MP.g, MN.g
  net out [electrical]: out, MP.d, MN.d
  net vdd [electrical]: vdd, MP.s, MP.b
  net vss [electrical]: vss, MN.s, MN.b

circuit buffer
  ports: a (inout, electrical), y (inout, electrical), vdd (inout, electrical), vss (inout, electrical)

items.title: Spectre with SPICE blocks
items.text:
Spectre decks often switch language with simulator lang=.... The spectre_spice parser handles both halves in one file:

SPECTRE_SPICE = """\
simulator lang=spice
.subckt rdiv a b mid
R1 a mid 1k
R2 mid b 1k
.ends rdiv

simulator lang=spectre
subckt top (vin gnd)
X0 (vin gnd tap) rdiv
C0 (tap gnd) capacitor c=1p
ends top
"""
spectre_spice = parse_spectre_spice(SPECTRE_SPICE)
summary(spectre_spice)

top circuit: top
external circuit: resistor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'R'}
external circuit: capacitor(p, n) {'spice_prefix': 'C'}

circuit rdiv

  instance R1: resistor  value=1k
  instance R2: resistor  value=1k
  net a [electrical]: a, R1.p
  net b [electrical]: b, R2.n
  net mid [electrical]: mid, R1.n, R2.p

  ports: vin (inout, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)

  net gnd [electrical]: gnd, X0.b, C0.n

items.title: Verilog-AMS
items.text:
Verilog-AMS modules declare port directions and disciplines (the discipline is kept as Port.discipline). analog blocks are not structure: they are kept as text in the circuit's analog_block property.

VAMS = """\
`include "disciplines.vams"
module res_model (p, n);
  inout p, n;
  electrical p, n;
  parameter real r = 1k;
  analog V(p, n) <+ r * I(p, n);
endmodule

module divider (vin, vout, gnd);
  input vin;
  output vout;
  inout gnd;
  electrical vin, vout, gnd;
  res_model #(.r(10k)) R1 (.p(vin), .n(vout));
  res_model #(.r(10k)) R2 (.p(vout), .n(gnd));
endmodule
"""
vams = parse_vams(VAMS)
summary(vams)

top circuit: divider
directive: INCLUDE disciplines.vams

circuit res_model
  parameters: r=1k
  ports: p (inout, electrical), n (inout, electrical)
  analog_block: analog V(p, n) <+ r * I(p, n);

circuit divider
  ports: vin (input, electrical), vout (output, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)
  instance R1: res_model  r=10k
  instance R2: res_model  r=10k
  net vin [electrical]: vin, R1.p
  net vout [electrical]: vout, R1.n, R2.p
  net gnd [electrical]: gnd, R2.n

items.title: SystemVerilog
items.text:
The SystemVerilog parser reads the structural part of the language (SystemVerilog 3.1a, Annex A):

  • ANSI headers (input wire [3:0] a, output y) and non-ANSI port lists with body declarations;
  • parameter/localparam, also in the #(...) header; numbers, sized literals (4'b1010) and expressions (kept as text in an expr property);
  • instances with named .p(n), positional, implicit .p, wildcard .* and empty .p() connections, several per statement;
  • assign a = b; and alias a = b = c;, which merge nets.

Behavioral code (always, initial, function, task, generate, class, assign with logic on the right, ...) is kept as text in behavioral_block_N properties.

SYSTEMVERILOG = """\
`timescale 1ns/1ps
module nand2 (input a, b, output y, inout vdd, vss);
  pmos_t P1 (.d(y), .g(a), .s(vdd)), P2 (.d(y), .g(b), .s(vdd));
  nmos_t N1 (.d(y), .g(a), .s(mid)), N2 (.d(mid), .g(b), .s(vss));
endmodule

module latch (s_n, r_n, q, q_n, vdd, vss);
  input s_n, r_n;
  output q, q_n;
  inout vdd, vss;
  wire qi;
  nand2 U1 (.a(s_n), .b(q_n), .y(qi), .*);
  nand2 U2 (.a(r_n), .b(q), .y(q_n), .*);
  assign q = qi;
  initial $display("latch ready");
endmodule
"""
systemverilog = parse_systemverilog(SYSTEMVERILOG)
summary(systemverilog)

top circuit: latch
directive: TIMESCALE 1ns/1ps

circuit nand2
  ports: a (input, electrical), b (input, electrical), y (output, electrical), vdd (inout, electrical), vss (inout, electrical)

  instance P2: pmos_t

  net b [electrical]: b, P2.g, N2.g
  net y [electrical]: y, P1.d, P2.d, N1.d

items.title: Photonic circuits
items.text:
The same parsers read photonic netlists. Terminals named o<N> are waveguide terminals; heater and bias pins (e1, vdd, ...) stay electrical. A Mach-Zehnder interferometer with a thermal phase shifter, in SystemVerilog:

MZI_SV = """\
module mzi #(parameter real arm_length = 100e-6) (
  input o1, o2, output o3, o4,   // optical
  input e1, inout gnd            // heater drive
);
  dc #(.gap(200n)) Xdc1 (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(top_a), .o4(bot_a));
  dc #(.gap(200n)) Xdc2 (.o1(top_b), .o2(bot_b), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
  heater_wg #(.length(arm_length)) Xtop (.o1(top_a), .o2(top_b), .e1(e1), .e2(gnd));
  wg #(.length(arm_length)) Xbot (.o1(bot_a), .o2(bot_b));
endmodule
"""
mzi_sv = parse_systemverilog(MZI_SV)
summary(mzi_sv)

top circuit: mzi

circuit mzi
  parameters: arm_length=0.0001
  ports: o1 (input, waveguide), o2 (input, waveguide), o3 (output, waveguide), o4 (output, waveguide), e1 (input, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)
  instance Xdc1: dc  gap=200n
  instance Xdc2: dc  gap=200n
  instance Xtop: heater_wg  length=arm_length
  instance Xbot: wg  length=arm_length
  net o1 [waveguide]: o1, Xdc1.o1
  net o2 [waveguide]: o2, Xdc1.o2
  net o3 [waveguide]: o3, Xdc2.o3
  net o4 [waveguide]: o4, Xdc2.o4
  net e1 [electrical]: e1, Xtop.e1
  net gnd [electrical]: gnd, Xtop.e2
  net top_a [waveguide]: Xdc1.o3, Xtop.o1
  net bot_a [waveguide]: Xdc1.o4, Xbot.o1
  net top_b [waveguide]: Xdc2.o1, Xtop.o2
  net bot_b [waveguide]: Xdc2.o2, Xbot.o2

The same MZI as a SPICE subcircuit. SPICE has no port names on subcircuit calls, so the instance pins of undeclared subcircuits are numbered and only the nets that reach an o<N> terminal of mzi itself are waveguide. Define the subcircuits in the deck (as here) and every net keeps its domain:

MZI_SPICE = """\
.subckt dc o1 o2 o3 o4 gap=200n
.ends dc
.subckt wg o1 o2 length=100u
.ends wg
.subckt heater_wg o1 o2 e1 e2 length=100u
.ends heater_wg
.subckt mzi o1 o2 o3 o4 e1 gnd
Xdc1 o1 o2 top_a bot_a dc
Xdc2 top_b bot_b o3 o4 dc
Xtop top_a top_b e1 gnd heater_wg
Xbot bot_a bot_b wg
.ends mzi
"""
mzi_spice = parse_spice(MZI_SPICE)
summary(mzi_spice)

top circuit: mzi

circuit dc
  parameters: gap=200n
  ports: o1 (inout, waveguide), o2 (inout, waveguide), o3 (inout, waveguide), o4 (inout, waveguide)

circuit wg
  parameters: length=100u
  ports: o1 (inout, waveguide), o2 (inout, waveguide)

circuit heater_wg
  parameters: length=100u
  ports: o1 (inout, waveguide), o2 (inout, waveguide), e1 (inout, electrical), e2 (inout, electrical)

circuit mzi
  ports: o1 (inout, waveguide), o2 (inout, waveguide), o3 (inout, waveguide), o4 (inout, waveguide), e1 (inout, electrical), gnd (inout, electrical)
  instance Xdc1: dc

  net o2 [waveguide]: o2, Xdc1.o2

items.title: Defining a netlist in Python
items.text:
Netlists can also be built directly with the morphnet builder API (see Basic Usage), and then written in any format:

from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist import write_systemverilog

WG = morphnet.SignalDomain.WAVEGUIDE
ring = morphnet.circuit("ring_filter", parameters=[("radius", 10e-6)])
for name in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"):
    ring.add_terminal(name, domain=WG)
ring.add(morphnet.subcircuit("Xring", "ring_coupler", gap=150e-9))
for name in ("o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"):
    ring.connect(name, ("", name), ("Xring", name), domain=WG)

doc = morphnet.Netlist(name="ring", top_circuit="ring_filter").add(ring)
summary(doc)
print()
print(write_systemverilog(doc))

top circuit: ring_filter

circuit ring_filter
  parameters: radius=1e-05
  ports: o1 (inout, waveguide), o2 (inout, waveguide), o3 (inout, waveguide), o4 (inout, waveguide)
  instance Xring: ring_coupler  gap=1.5e-07
  net o1 [waveguide]: o1, Xring.o1
  net o2 [waveguide]: o2, Xring.o2
  net o3 [waveguide]: o3, Xring.o3
  net o4 [waveguide]: o4, Xring.o4

module ring_filter #(parameter radius = 1e-05) (
  inout o1,
  inout o2,
  inout o3,
  inout o4
);
  ring_coupler #(.gap(1.5e-07)) Xring (.o1(o1), .o2(o2), .o3(o3), .o4(o4));
endmodule

items.title: Ring oscillator: build once, export to every format
items.text:
A hierarchical CMOS ring oscillator built with the kfnetlist.morphnet builder API, then written as SPICE, HSPICE, Xyce, Spectre, Verilog-AMS and YAML, and parsed back to show the conversion is bidirectional.

Adapted from morphnet's examples/inverter.py. The changes:

  • The nfet/pfet external circuits declare their ports, so positional formats (SPICE, Spectre) know the pin order.
  • Nets that reach a circuit terminal are named after it. A subcircuit port is wired to the node with the same name.
  • Instance names follow SPICE's first-letter convention: X marks a subcircuit or PDK-cell call. Without it, inv1 would read as a current source.
from kfnetlist import morphnet
from kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist import (
    parse_hspice,
    parse_spectre,
    parse_spice,
    parse_vams,
    parse_xyce,
    write_hspice,
    write_spectre,
    write_spice,
    write_vams,
    write_xyce,
)

items.title: Leaf inverter cell
items.text:
circuit() declares a circuit and its parameters (names only, or (name, default) tuples). add_terminal() adds the circuit's I/O, subcircuit() places sub-instances with parameter overrides as keyword arguments, and connect() names a net and lists its endpoints. ("", terminal) is the circuit's own terminal.

inv = morphnet.circuit("inverter", parameters=["l", "w"])
inv.add_terminal("vdd", direction=morphnet.PortDirection.INPUT)
inv.add_terminal("gnd", direction=morphnet.PortDirection.INPUT)
inv.add_terminal("inp", direction=morphnet.PortDirection.INPUT)
inv.add_terminal("out", direction=morphnet.PortDirection.OUTPUT)

inv.add(
    morphnet.subcircuit("XMN", "nfet", l=100e-9, w=500e-9),
    morphnet.subcircuit("XMP", "pfet", l=100e-9, w=1000e-9),
)

inv.connect("out", ("XMN", "drain"), ("XMP", "drain"), ("", "out"))
inv.connect("inp", ("", "inp"), ("XMN", "gate"), ("XMP", "gate"))
inv.connect("vdd", ("", "vdd"), ("XMP", "source"))
inv.connect("gnd", ("", "gnd"), ("XMN", "source"))

items.title: Netlist: PDK library, device models, circuits
items.text:
external_library() points at the model file, and ext_circuit() declares the devices it provides, including their pin order.

fet_ports = [morphnet.port(name) for name in ("drain", "gate", "source")]

ckt = morphnet.Netlist(name="ring_osc_top", top_circuit="ring_osc")
ckt.add_library(
    "tt",
    morphnet.external_library(
        "path/to/tt.lib", model_type="tt", external_model_names=["nfet", "pfet"]
    ),
)

items.title: Parse it back
items.text:
Every format parses back into a morphnet Netlist. Converting each one to kfnetlist.Netlist graphs shows that the connectivity survived every round trip.

Positional formats (the SPICE family and Spectre) record pin order, not pin names, so their instance pins come back as p0, p1, and so on. Only Verilog-AMS keeps the names. The check below therefore compares pins by position.

from kfnetlist import NetlistPort  # noqa: E402

PARSERS = {
    "SPICE": parse_spice,
    "HSPICE": parse_hspice,
    "Xyce": parse_xyce,
    "Spectre": parse_spectre,
    "Verilog-AMS": parse_vams,
}
pin_order = {m.name: [p.name for p in m.ports] for m in [*ckt.circuits, *ckt.ext_circuits]}
cell_of = {r.name: r.circuit_name for m in ckt.circuits for r in m.subcircuits}


def pin(member) -> str:
    if isinstance(member, NetlistPort):
        return f"<{member.name}>"
    pins = pin_order[cell_of[member.instance]]
    index = pins.index(member.port) if member.port in pins else int(member.port[1:])
    return f"{member.instance}[{index}]"


def connectivity(netlist: morphnet.Netlist) -> dict[str, list[list[str]]]:
    return {
        name: sorted(sorted(map(pin, net)) for net in nl.nets)
        for name, nl in morphnet.to_netlists(netlist).items()
    }


reference = connectivity(ckt)
for fmt, parse in PARSERS.items():
    assert connectivity(parse(texts[fmt])) == reference, fmt
    print(f"{fmt}: connectivity preserved")

HSPICE: connectivity preserved


Xyce: connectivity preserved
Spectre: connectivity preserved

check_connection(
    p1: PortLike,
    p2: PortLike,
    *,
    tolerance: float = 0.1,
    angle_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    snapped: bool = False,
) -> int

Compare two ports, returning a :class:PortCheck bitmask.

Integer transforms are used when both ports expose trans (or when snapped=True); otherwise the complex transforms are used with the supplied tolerances. cross_section implies layer and width.

Source code in src/kfnetlist/port_check.py 
def check_connection(
    p1: PortLike,
    p2: PortLike,
    *,
    tolerance: float = 0.1,
    angle_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    snapped: bool = False,
) -> int:
    """Compare two ports, returning a :class:`PortCheck` bitmask.

    Integer transforms are used when both ports expose ``trans`` (or when
    ``snapped=True``); otherwise the complex transforms are used with the
    supplied tolerances. ``cross_section`` implies ``layer`` and ``width``.
    """
    tol_um = p1.kcl.dbu * tolerance
    check = 0
    if snapped or (p1.trans is not None and p2.trans is not None):
        t1 = _get_trans(p1)
        t2 = _get_trans(p2)
        if t1.disp == t2.disp:
            check += PortCheck.position
        orientation = (t1.angle - t2.angle) % 4
        if orientation == 2:
            check += PortCheck.opposite
        elif orientation == 0:
            check += PortCheck.same
    else:
        dt1 = _get_dcplx_trans(p1)
        dt2 = _get_dcplx_trans(p2)
        if (dt1.disp - dt2.disp).length() < tol_um:
            check += PortCheck.position
        angle_diff = (dt1.angle - dt2.angle) % 360
        if abs(angle_diff - 180) < angle_tolerance:
            check += PortCheck.opposite
        elif abs(angle_diff) < angle_tolerance:
            check += PortCheck.same
    if p1.cross_section == p2.cross_section:
        check += PortCheck.cross_section
        check += PortCheck.layer
        check += PortCheck.width
    else:
        if p1.cross_section.main_layer.is_equivalent(p2.cross_section.main_layer):
            check += PortCheck.layer
        if p1.cross_section.width == p2.cross_section.width:
            check += PortCheck.width
    if p1.port_type == p2.port_type:
        check += PortCheck.port_type
    return check

def connections_to_instance_nets(
    connections: list[Connection],
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], str]:
    """Build (instance_name, port_name) → net_name lookup from Connection objects.

    Single pass over connections — O(n).  Used by writers to reconstruct
    instance lines with the correct net names in port order.
    """
    mapping: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
    for conn in connections:
        net_name = conn.name
        if conn.source is not None:
            key = (conn.source.instance_name, conn.source.port_name)
            mapping[key] = net_name
        if conn.target is not None:
            key = (conn.target.instance_name, conn.target.port_name)
            mapping[key] = net_name
    return mapping

items.title: net_map_to_connections
items.text:
net_map_to_connections(net_map: NetMap) -> list[Connection]

Convert a net-based connectivity map to point-to-point Connection objects.

For each net with N port references, produces N-1 Connection objects. The first port reference (in insertion order) becomes the source for all connections on that net.

Complexity: O(n) where n = total port references across all nets.

Source code in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/net_utils.py 
def net_map_to_connections(net_map: NetMap) -> list[Connection]:
    """Convert a net-based connectivity map to point-to-point Connection objects.

    For each net with N port references, produces N-1 Connection objects.
    The first port reference (in insertion order) becomes the source for
    all connections on that net.

    Complexity: O(n) where n = total port references across all nets.
    """
    connections: list[Connection] = []
    for net_name, port_refs in net_map.items():
        if len(port_refs) < 2:
            continue
        source = port_refs[0]
        domain = (
            SignalDomain.WAVEGUIDE
            if any(domain_of(r.port_name) == SignalDomain.WAVEGUIDE for r in port_refs)
            else SignalDomain.ELECTRICAL
        )
        for target in port_refs[1:]:
            connections.append(
                Connection(
                    name=net_name,
                    source=source,
                    target=target,
                    domain=domain,
                )
            )
    return connections

Prepare HSPICE text for Lark parsing.

def preprocess_hspice(text: str) -> str:
    """Prepare HSPICE text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip comment lines (* at column 0) and inline comments ($ or ;).
    2. Join backslash continuations (\\ at end of line).
    3. Join + continuations (+ at start of next line).
    4. Ensure trailing newline.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("*"):
            continue
        cleaned = strip_inline_comment(stripped)
        if not cleaned:
            continue
        lines.append(cleaned)

    joined_lines = join_continuations_backslash(lines).splitlines()
    joined = join_continuations(joined_lines)
    if joined and not joined.endswith("\n"):
        joined += "\n"
    return joined

Prepare Spectre text for Lark parsing.

  1. Strip block comments (/ ... /) and line comments (//).
  2. Join backslash-continuation lines.
  3. Collapse whitespace, ensure trailing newline.
Source code in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/spectre/preprocess.py 
def preprocess_spectre(text: str) -> str:
    """Prepare Spectre text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip block comments (/* ... */) and line comments (//).
    2. Join backslash-continuation lines.
    3. Collapse whitespace, ensure trailing newline.
    """
    text = BLOCK_COMMENT_RE.sub("", text)

    lines: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        idx = stripped.find("//")
        if idx >= 0:
            stripped = stripped[:idx].rstrip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        lines.append(stripped)

    joined = join_continuations_backslash(lines)
    result = add_semicolons(joined)
    if result and not result.endswith("\n"):
        result += "\n"
    return result

def preprocess_spectre_spice(text: str) -> list[SpectreSpiceSection]:
    """Split a Spectre-SPICE file into sections by language mode.

    Default mode is 'spice'. Lines matching 'simulator lang=spectre'
    or 'simulator lang=spice' switch the mode.
    """
    sections: list[SpectreSpiceSection] = []
    current_lang = "spice"
    current_lines: list[str] = []

    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = SIMULATOR_LANG_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            if current_lines:
                sections.append(
                    SpectreSpiceSection(
                        language=current_lang,
                        text="\n".join(current_lines) + "\n",
                    )
                )
                current_lines = []
            current_lang = m.group(1).lower()
        else:
            current_lines.append(line)

    if current_lines:
        sections.append(
            SpectreSpiceSection(
                language=current_lang,
                text="\n".join(current_lines) + "\n",
            )
        )

    return sections

def preprocess_spice(text: str) -> str:
    """Prepare SPICE/HSPICE text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip comment lines (* at column 0) and inline comments ($ or ;).
    2. Join continuation lines (+ at start of next line appends to previous).
    3. Collapse runs of whitespace to single spaces, strip trailing whitespace.
    4. Ensure a trailing newline.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("*"):
            continue
        cleaned = strip_inline_comment(stripped)
        if not cleaned:
            continue
        lines.append(cleaned)

    joined = join_continuations(lines)
    if joined and not joined.endswith("\n"):
        joined += "\n"
    return joined

def preprocess_systemverilog(text: str) -> SvPreprocessResult:
    """Prepare SystemVerilog text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip block comments, line comments and ``(* attributes *)``.
    2. Extract backtick directives (`include, `define, `timescale, etc.).
    3. Replace behavioral constructs (always, initial, function, task, generate,
       class, non-trivial assign, ...) with ``__sv_placeholder__ N ;`` markers.
       typedef / import / genvar / timeunit statements are dropped.
    """
    text = BLOCK_COMMENT_RE.sub("", text)
    text = LINE_COMMENT_RE.sub("", text)
    text = ATTRIBUTE_RE.sub("", text)

    directives = [(m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()) for m in DIRECTIVE_RE.finditer(text)]
    text = DIRECTIVE_RE.sub("", text)

    text, blocks = replace_behavioral_blocks(text)

    text = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n", text).strip()
    if text:
        text += "\n"
    return SvPreprocessResult(text=text, directives=directives, blocks=blocks)

def format_si_value(pv: PrefixedValue) -> str:
    """Format a PrefixedValue as a SPICE-style string like '10k', '2.2u'.

    Produces the shortest clean representation (no trailing zeros).
    """
    num = pv.double_value
    if num == int(num):
        num_str = str(int(num))
    else:
        num_str = f"{num:g}"

    if pv.prefix == SIPrefix.UNSPECIFIED:
        return num_str

    suffix = PREFIX_TO_SI_SUFFIX.get(pv.prefix, "")
    return f"{num_str}{suffix}"

Parse a SPICE-style SI-prefixed number like '10k', '2.2u', '100meg'.

Returns a PrefixedValue with the numeric part and the SIPrefix enum. Raises ValueError if the token is not a valid SI number.

Source code in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/value_utils.py 
def parse_si_number(token: str) -> PrefixedValue:
    """Parse a SPICE-style SI-prefixed number like '10k', '2.2u', '100meg'.

    Returns a PrefixedValue with the numeric part and the SIPrefix enum.
    Raises ValueError if the token is not a valid SI number.
    """
    m = SI_NUMBER_RE.match(token)
    if m is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Not a valid SI number: {token!r}")
    numeric_str, suffix = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    value = float(numeric_str)
    if suffix is None:
        prefix = SIPrefix.UNSPECIFIED
    else:
        suffix_lower = suffix.lower()
        if suffix_lower == "mil":
            return PrefixedValue(
                double_value=value * MIL_SCALE, prefix=SIPrefix.UNSPECIFIED
            )
        prefix = SI_SUFFIX_TO_PREFIX.get(suffix_lower)
        if prefix is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown SI suffix: {suffix!r}")
    return PrefixedValue(double_value=value, prefix=prefix)

    """Prepare HSPICE text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip comment lines (* at column 0) and inline comments ($ or ;).
    2. Join backslash continuations (\\ at end of line).
    3. Join + continuations (+ at start of next line).
    4. Ensure trailing newline.

Append semicolons to lines that are not block openers/closers.

Spectre uses newlines as statement terminators. For LALR parsing we inject explicit semicolons so the grammar can ignore all whitespace. Block-opening lines (subckt, section) and block-closing lines (ends, endsection) get their own markers handled by the grammar directly.

def add_semicolons(text: str) -> str:
    """Append semicolons to lines that are not block openers/closers.

    Spectre uses newlines as statement terminators. For LALR parsing we
    inject explicit semicolons so the grammar can ignore all whitespace.
    Block-opening lines (subckt, section) and block-closing lines (ends,
    endsection) get their own markers handled by the grammar directly.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        first_word = stripped.split()[0] if stripped.split() else ""
        if first_word in BLOCK_KEYWORDS or first_word in END_KEYWORDS:
            out.append(stripped)
        else:
            out.append(stripped + " ;")
    return "\n".join(out)

def join_continuations_backslash(lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """Join backslash-continuation lines (trailing \\ merges with next line)."""
    if not lines:
        return ""
    merged: list[str] = []
    buf = ""
    for line in lines:
        if line.endswith("\\"):
            buf += line[:-1].rstrip() + " "
        else:
            buf += line
            merged.append(buf)
            buf = ""
    if buf:
        merged.append(buf)
    return "\n".join(merged)

  1. Strip block comments (/ ... /) and line comments (//).

def preprocess_spectre(text: str) -> str:
    """Prepare Spectre text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip block comments (/* ... */) and line comments (//).
    2. Join backslash-continuation lines.
    3. Collapse whitespace, ensure trailing newline.
    """
    text = BLOCK_COMMENT_RE.sub("", text)

    lines: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        idx = stripped.find("//")
        if idx >= 0:
            stripped = stripped[:idx].rstrip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        lines.append(stripped)

    joined = join_continuations_backslash(lines)
    result = add_semicolons(joined)
    if result and not result.endswith("\n"):
        result += "\n"
    return result

class SpectreTransformer(Transformer[Token, Netlist]):
    """Transform a Spectre parse tree into a Netlist model."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.all_subckts: dict[str, Circuit] = {}

    # ── Leaf transformers ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    def net_ref(self, items: list[Token]) -> str:
        return str(items[0])

    def pvalue_number(self, items: list[Token]) -> ParameterValue:
        return parse_parameter_number(str(items[0]))

    def pvalue_ident(self, items: list[Token]) -> ParameterValue:
        return ParameterValue()

    def pvalue_string(self, items: list[Token]) -> ParameterValue:
        return ParameterValue()

    def param_assign(self, items: list[Any]) -> tuple[str, ParameterValue]:
        name = str(items[0])
        value = items[1]
        if not isinstance(value, ParameterValue):
            value = ParameterValue()
        return (name, value)

    def port_decl(self, items: list[Token]) -> tuple[str, str]:
        return ("__port__", str(items[0]))

    # ── Instance statement ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    def instance_stmt(self, items: list[Any]) -> InstanceData | AnalysisData:
        inst_name = str(items[0])
        device_prefix = inst_name[0].upper()

        net_names: list[str] = []
        cell_name = ""
        params: dict[str, ParameterValue] = {}

        for item in items[1:]:
            if isinstance(item, Token):
                cell_name = str(item)
            elif isinstance(item, tuple):
                pname, pval = item
                if isinstance(pval, ParameterValue):
                    params[pname] = pval
            elif isinstance(item, str):
                net_names.append(item)

        # A subckt defined in the deck named like an analysis (`dc`) is an instance
        if cell_name in SPECTRE_ANALYSIS_TYPES and cell_name not in self.all_subckts:
            opts: dict[str, str] = {}
            for pname, pval in params.items():
                opts[pname] = _param_value_to_str(pval)
            return AnalysisData(
                kind=cell_name, name=inst_name, arguments=[], options=opts
            )

        return InstanceData(
            name=inst_name,
            net_names=net_names,
            cell_name=cell_name,
            params=params,
            device_prefix=device_prefix,
        )

    # ── model statement ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def model_stmt(self, items: list[Any]) -> ModelData:
        name = str(items[0])
        type_name = str(items[1])
        params: dict[str, ParameterValue] = {}
        for item in items[2:]:
            if isinstance(item, tuple):
                pname, pval = item
                if isinstance(pval, ParameterValue):
                    params[pname] = pval
        return ModelData(name=name, type_name=type_name, params=params)

    # ── parameters statement ────────────────────────────────────────────

    def parameters_stmt(self, items: list[Any]) -> ParamData:
        params: dict[str, ParameterValue] = {}
        for item in items:
            if isinstance(item, tuple):
                pname, pval = item
                if isinstance(pval, ParameterValue):
                    params[pname] = pval
        return ParamData(params=params)

    # ── include ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def include_stmt(self, items: list[Any]) -> IncludeData:
        path = str(items[0]).strip("\"'")
        return IncludeData(path=path)

    # ── save statement ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def save_stmt(self, items: list[Any]) -> OutputRequestData:
        variables = [str(item) for item in items if isinstance(item, str)]
        return OutputRequestData(kind="save", analysis_type="", variables=variables)

    # ── section (pass through body) ─────────────────────────────────────

    def section_body(self, items: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
        return [i for i in items if i is not None]

    def section_def(self, items: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
        # Return body items to be merged into parent
        for item in items:
            if isinstance(item, list):
                return item
        return []

    # ── Subcircuit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def subckt_body(self, items: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
        return [i for i in items if i is not None]

    def subckt_def(self, items: list[Any]) -> SubcktData:
        subckt_name = str(items[0])

        port_names: list[str] = []
        subckt_params: dict[str, ParameterValue] = {}
        body_items: list[Any] = []

        for item in items[1:]:
            if isinstance(item, tuple) and len(item) == 2 and item[0] == "__port__":
                port_names.append(item[1])
            elif isinstance(item, tuple) and len(item) == 2 and item[0] != "__port__":
                pname, pval = item
                if isinstance(pval, ParameterValue):
                    subckt_params[pname] = pval
            elif isinstance(item, list):
                body_items = item

        result = self.build_subckt(subckt_name, port_names, subckt_params, body_items)
        self.all_subckts[subckt_name] = result.circuit
        return result

    def build_subckt(
        self,
        name: str,
        port_names: list[str],
        subckt_params: dict[str, ParameterValue],
        body_items: list[Any],
    ) -> SubcktData:
        instances: list[InstanceData] = []
        nested_subckts: dict[str, Circuit] = {}
        ext_circuits: dict[str, ExternalCircuit] = {}
        model_defs: dict[str, ModelData] = {}
        circuit_params: list[Parameter] = []
        directives: list[Directive] = []

        for item in body_items:
            if isinstance(item, InstanceData):
                instances.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, SubcktData):
                nested_subckts[item.circuit.name] = item.circuit
                ext_circuits.update(item.ext_circuits)
            elif isinstance(item, ModelData):
                model_defs[item.name] = item
            elif isinstance(item, ParamData):
                for pname, pval in item.params.items():
                    circuit_params.append(Parameter(name=pname, default_value=pval))
            elif isinstance(item, IncludeData):
                directives.append(
                    Directive(kind=DirectiveKind.INCLUDE, value=item.path)
                )
            elif isinstance(item, list):
                for sub_item in item:
                    if isinstance(sub_item, InstanceData):
                        instances.append(sub_item)

        for pname, pval in subckt_params.items():
            circuit_params.append(Parameter(name=pname, default_value=pval))

        ports: list[Port] = [
            Port(
                name=pn,
                direction=PortDirection.INOUT,
                domain=domain_of(pn),
            )
            for pn in port_names
        ]

        net_map: NetMap = {}
        subcircuits: list[SubCircuit] = []

        for port in ports:
            add_port_to_net(net_map, port.name, "", port.name)

        for inst in instances:
            # Spectre picks the device from the master, not the instance name:
            # a defined subckt or a built-in master (`capacitor`) wins over the
            # SPICE-style name prefix, which is only the fallback.
            subckt_mod = nested_subckts.get(inst.cell_name) or self.all_subckts.get(
                inst.cell_name
            )
            device_prefix = CIRCUIT_TO_PREFIX.get(inst.cell_name, inst.device_prefix)
            port_template = DEVICE_PORT_TEMPLATES.get(device_prefix)

            # In Spectre, nets and cell name are already separated by grammar
            if subckt_mod is not None or device_prefix == "X" or port_template is None:
                # Subcircuit or unknown: resolve ports from definition
                if subckt_mod is not None:
                    inst_port_names = [p.name for p in subckt_mod.ports]
                else:
                    inst_port_names = [f"p{i}" for i in range(len(inst.net_names))]

                for net_name, port_name in zip(inst.net_names, inst_port_names):
                    add_port_to_net(net_map, net_name, inst.name, port_name)

                subcircuits.append(
                    SubCircuit(
                        name=inst.name,
                        circuit_name=inst.cell_name,
                        parameters=[
                            Parameter(name=pname, default_value=pval)
                            for pname, pval in inst.params.items()
                        ],
                    )
                )
            else:
                # Known primitive device
                module_name = DEVICE_PREFIX_TO_CIRCUIT.get(
                    device_prefix, device_prefix.lower()
                )

                for net_name, port_name in zip(inst.net_names, port_template):
                    add_port_to_net(net_map, net_name, inst.name, port_name)

                if module_name not in ext_circuits:
                    ext_ports = [
                        Port(
                            name=pn,
                            direction=PortDirection.INOUT,
                            domain=domain_of(pn),
                        )
                        for pn in port_template
                    ]
                    ext_circuits[module_name] = ExternalCircuit(
                        name=module_name,
                        ports=ext_ports,
                        properties={"spice_prefix": device_prefix},
                    )

                params = [
                    Parameter(name=pname, default_value=pval)
                    for pname, pval in inst.params.items()
                ]
                props: dict[str, str] = {}
                if inst.cell_name and inst.cell_name != module_name:
                    props["model_name"] = inst.cell_name

                subcircuits.append(
                    SubCircuit(
                        name=inst.name,
                        circuit_name=module_name,
                        parameters=params,
                        properties=props,
                    )
                )

        for mdata in model_defs.values():
            if mdata.name not in ext_circuits:
                ext_circuits[mdata.name] = ExternalCircuit(
                    name=mdata.name,
                    parameters=[
                        Parameter(name=pn, default_value=pv)
                        for pn, pv in mdata.params.items()
                    ],
                    properties={"model_type": mdata.type_name},
                )

        connections = net_map_to_connections(net_map)

        circuit = Circuit(
            name=name,
            ports=ports,
            parameters=circuit_params,
            subcircuits=subcircuits,
            connections=connections,
            directives=directives,
        )
        return SubcktData(circuit=circuit, ext_circuits=ext_circuits)

    # ── Top-level ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def start(self, items: list[Any]) -> Netlist:
        subckt_datas: list[SubcktData] = []
        model_defs: dict[str, ModelData] = {}
        top_instances: list[InstanceData] = []
        directives: list[Directive] = []
        analyses: list[AnalysisData] = []
        output_requests: list[OutputRequestData] = []

        for item in items:
            if item is None:
                continue
            if isinstance(item, SubcktData):
                subckt_datas.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, ModelData):
                model_defs[item.name] = item
            elif isinstance(item, InstanceData):
                top_instances.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, AnalysisData):
                analyses.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, OutputRequestData):
                output_requests.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, IncludeData):
                directives.append(
                    Directive(kind=DirectiveKind.INCLUDE, value=item.path)
                )
            elif isinstance(item, ParamData):
                for pname, pval in item.params.items():
                    val = _param_value_to_str(pval)
                    directives.append(
                        Directive(kind=DirectiveKind.PARAM, name=pname, value=val)
                    )
            elif isinstance(item, list):
                for sub_item in item:
                    if isinstance(sub_item, SubcktData):
                        subckt_datas.append(sub_item)
                    elif isinstance(sub_item, AnalysisData):
                        analyses.append(sub_item)
                    elif isinstance(sub_item, OutputRequestData):
                        output_requests.append(sub_item)

        circuits: list[Circuit] = []
        all_ext_circuits: dict[str, ExternalCircuit] = {}

        for sd in subckt_datas:
            circuits.append(sd.circuit)
            all_ext_circuits.update(sd.ext_circuits)

        if top_instances:
            top_data = self.build_subckt("__top__", [], {}, top_instances)
            circuits.insert(0, top_data.circuit)
            all_ext_circuits.update(top_data.ext_circuits)

        for mdata in model_defs.values():
            if mdata.name not in all_ext_circuits:
                all_ext_circuits[mdata.name] = ExternalCircuit(
                    name=mdata.name,
                    parameters=[
                        Parameter(name=pn, default_value=pv)
                        for pn, pv in mdata.params.items()
                    ],
                    properties={"model_type": mdata.type_name},
                )

        top_circuit = circuits[-1].name if circuits else ""

        simulation: Simulation | None = None
        if analyses or output_requests:
            simulation = Simulation(
                analyses=[
                    Analysis(
                        kind=ANALYSIS_KIND_MAP.get(a.kind),
                        name=a.name,
                        arguments=a.arguments,
                        options=a.options,
                    )
                    for a in analyses
                ],
                output_requests=[
                    OutputRequest(
                        kind=OUTPUT_REQUEST_KIND_MAP.get(o.kind),
                        analysis_type=o.analysis_type,
                        variables=o.variables,
                    )
                    for o in output_requests
                ],
            )

        return Netlist(
            name="",
            top_circuit=top_circuit,
            circuits=circuits,
            ext_circuits=list(all_ext_circuits.values()),
            directives=directives,
            simulation=simulation,
        )

class SpectreWriter:
    """Convert a Netlist model to Spectre netlist text."""

    def format_param_value(self, pval: ParameterValue) -> str:
        """Format any ParameterValue variant as a Spectre-compatible string."""
        if pval.prefixed_value is not None:
            return format_si_value(pval.prefixed_value)
        return "0"

    def write(self, netlist: Netlist) -> str:
        lines: list[str] = []

        ext_by_name: dict[str, ExternalCircuit] = {
            e.name: e for e in netlist.ext_circuits
        }
        circuit_by_name: dict[str, Circuit] = {m.name: m for m in netlist.circuits}

        self.write_directives(netlist.directives, lines)

        for ext in netlist.ext_circuits:
            model_type = ext.properties.get("model_type")
            if model_type:
                self.write_model(ext, model_type, lines)

        for circuit in netlist.circuits:
            if circuit.name == "__top__":
                self.write_top_instances(circuit, ext_by_name, circuit_by_name, lines)
            else:
                self.write_subckt(circuit, ext_by_name, circuit_by_name, lines)

        if netlist.simulation:
            self.write_simulation(netlist.simulation, lines)

        lines.append("")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def write_directives(self, directives: list[Directive], lines: list[str]) -> None:
        params: dict[str, str] = {}
        for d in directives:
            if d.kind == DirectiveKind.INCLUDE:
                lines.append(f'include "{d.value}"')
            elif d.kind == DirectiveKind.PARAM:
                params[d.name] = d.value
        if params:
            assigns = " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in params.items())
            lines.append(f"parameters {assigns}")

    def write_model(
        self, ext: ExternalCircuit, model_type: str, lines: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        param_strs: list[str] = []
        for p in ext.parameters:
            if p.default_value:
                param_strs.append(
                    f"{p.name}={self.format_param_value(p.default_value)}"
                )
        params_text = " ".join(param_strs)
        lines.append(f"model {ext.name} {model_type} ({params_text})")

    def write_subckt(
        self,
        circuit: Circuit,
        ext_by_name: dict[str, ExternalCircuit],
        circuit_by_name: dict[str, Circuit],
        lines: list[str],
    ) -> None:
        port_names = " ".join(p.name for p in circuit.ports)

        param_strs: list[str] = []
        for param in circuit.parameters:
            if param.default_value:
                param_strs.append(
                    f"{param.name}={self.format_param_value(param.default_value)}"
                )
        params_suffix = " " + " ".join(param_strs) if param_strs else ""

        lines.append(f"subckt {circuit.name} ({port_names}){params_suffix}")

        inst_nets = connections_to_instance_nets(circuit.connections)

        for ref in circuit.subcircuits:
            lines.append(
                self.write_instance(ref, inst_nets, ext_by_name, circuit_by_name)
            )

        lines.append(f"ends {circuit.name}")

    def write_top_instances(
        self,
        circuit: Circuit,
        ext_by_name: dict[str, ExternalCircuit],
        circuit_by_name: dict[str, Circuit],
        lines: list[str],
    ) -> None:
        inst_nets = connections_to_instance_nets(circuit.connections)
        for ref in circuit.subcircuits:
            lines.append(
                self.write_instance(ref, inst_nets, ext_by_name, circuit_by_name)
            )

    def write_instance(
        self,
        ref: SubCircuit,
        inst_nets: dict[tuple[str, str], str],
        ext_by_name: dict[str, ExternalCircuit],
        circuit_by_name: dict[str, Circuit],
    ) -> str:
        ext_circuit = ext_by_name.get(ref.circuit_name)
        prefix = CIRCUIT_TO_PREFIX.get(ref.circuit_name)

        # Determine port order
        if prefix and ext_circuit:
            port_order = [p.name for p in ext_circuit.ports]
        else:
            ref_circuit = circuit_by_name.get(ref.circuit_name)
            if ref_circuit:
                port_order = [p.name for p in ref_circuit.ports]
            elif ext_circuit:
                port_order = [p.name for p in ext_circuit.ports]
            elif prefix:
                port_order = DEVICE_PORT_TEMPLATES[prefix]
            else:
                port_order = self.infer_port_order(ref, inst_nets)

        nets = [inst_nets.get((ref.name, pn), "?") for pn in port_order]
        nets_str = " ".join(nets)

        cell_name = ref.properties.get("model_name") or ref.circuit_name

        # Params
        param_strs: list[str] = []
        for param in ref.parameters:
            if param.default_value:
                param_strs.append(
                    f"{param.name}={self.format_param_value(param.default_value)}"
                )

        params_text = " " + " ".join(param_strs) if param_strs else ""
        return f"{ref.name} ({nets_str}) {cell_name}{params_text}"

    def infer_port_order(
        self,
        ref: SubCircuit,
        inst_nets: dict[tuple[str, str], str],
    ) -> list[str]:
        port_names: list[str] = []
        for iname, pname in inst_nets:
            if iname == ref.name and pname not in port_names:
                port_names.append(pname)
        return port_names

    # ── Simulation writing ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    def write_simulation(self, simulation: Simulation, lines: list[str]) -> None:
        for analysis in simulation.analyses:
            lines.append(self.format_analysis(analysis))
        for req in simulation.output_requests:
            lines.append(self.format_output_request(req))

    def format_analysis(self, analysis: Analysis) -> str:
        keyword = _ANALYSIS_KIND_TO_SPECTRE.get(analysis.kind, "dc")
        parts = [analysis.name or keyword, keyword]
        for k, v in analysis.options.items():
            parts.append(f"{k}={v}")
        return " ".join(parts)

    def format_output_request(self, req: OutputRequest) -> str:
        if req.kind == OutputRequestKind.SAVE:
            return "save " + " ".join(req.variables)
        return "save " + " ".join(req.variables)

Splits input on simulator lang= directives and delegates each section to the appropriate sub-parser.

Source code in src/kfnetlist/morphnet/netlist/spectre_spice/parser.py 
class SpectreSpiceParser:
    """Parse Spectre-SPICE netlist text into a Netlist model.

    Splits input on `simulator lang=` directives and delegates each
    section to the appropriate sub-parser.
    """

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Netlist:
        sections = preprocess_spectre_spice(text)

        all_circuits: list[Circuit] = []
        all_ext_circuits: dict[str, ExternalCircuit] = {}
        all_directives = []
        all_analyses: list[Analysis] = []
        all_output_requests: list[OutputRequest] = []
        all_measurements: list[Measurement] = []
        all_temperatures: list[float] = []
        ic_conditions: dict[str, str] = {}
        ns_conditions: dict[str, str] = {}

        section_of: dict[str, int] = {}
        for index, section in enumerate(sections):
            if not section.text.strip():
                continue
            if section.language == "spectre":
                netlist = parse_spectre(section.text)
            else:
                netlist = parse_spice(section.text)

            all_circuits.extend(netlist.circuits)
            section_of.update((c.name, index) for c in netlist.circuits)
            for ext in netlist.ext_circuits:
                all_ext_circuits[ext.name] = ext
            all_directives.extend(netlist.directives)

            if netlist.simulation:
                all_analyses.extend(netlist.simulation.analyses)
                all_output_requests.extend(netlist.simulation.output_requests)
                all_measurements.extend(netlist.simulation.measurements)
                all_temperatures.extend(netlist.simulation.temperatures)
                if netlist.simulation.initial_conditions:
                    ic_conditions.update(
                        netlist.simulation.initial_conditions.conditions
                    )
                if netlist.simulation.node_sets:
                    ns_conditions.update(netlist.simulation.node_sets.conditions)

        resolve_cross_section_pins(all_circuits, section_of)
        top_circuit = all_circuits[-1].name if all_circuits else ""

        has_sim = (
            all_analyses
            or all_output_requests
            or all_measurements
            or ic_conditions
            or ns_conditions
            or all_temperatures
        )
        simulation: Simulation | None = None
        if has_sim:
            simulation = Simulation(
                analyses=all_analyses,
                output_requests=all_output_requests,
                measurements=all_measurements,
                initial_conditions=(
                    InitialCondition(conditions=ic_conditions)
                    if ic_conditions
                    else None
                ),
                node_sets=(
                    InitialCondition(conditions=ns_conditions)
                    if ns_conditions
                    else None
                ),
                temperatures=all_temperatures,
            )

        return Netlist(
            name="",
            top_circuit=top_circuit,
            circuits=all_circuits,
            ext_circuits=list(all_ext_circuits.values()),
            directives=all_directives,
            simulation=simulation,
        )

Each section is parsed on its own, so such instances get positional p0, p1, ... pins; map them to the definition's port names.

def resolve_cross_section_pins(
    circuits: list[Circuit], section_of: dict[str, int]
) -> None:
    """Name the pins of instances whose subcircuit is defined in another section.

    Each section is parsed on its own, so such instances get positional ``p0``,
    ``p1``, ... pins; map them to the definition's port names.
    """
    ports = {c.name: [p.name for p in c.ports] for c in circuits}
    for circuit in circuits:
        targets = {
            s.name: ports[s.circuit_name]
            for s in circuit.subcircuits
            if s.circuit_name in ports
            and section_of[s.circuit_name] != section_of[circuit.name]
        }
        for conn in circuit.connections:
            for ref in (conn.source, conn.target):
                if ref is None or ref.instance_name not in targets:
                    continue
                m = POSITIONAL_PIN_RE.fullmatch(ref.port_name)
                names = targets[ref.instance_name]
                if m and int(m.group(1)) < len(names):
                    ref.port_name = names[int(m.group(1))]

def preprocess_spectre_spice(text: str) -> list[SpectreSpiceSection]:
    """Split a Spectre-SPICE file into sections by language mode.

    Default mode is 'spice'. Lines matching 'simulator lang=spectre'
    or 'simulator lang=spice' switch the mode.
    """
    sections: list[SpectreSpiceSection] = []
    current_lang = "spice"
    current_lines: list[str] = []

    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = SIMULATOR_LANG_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            if current_lines:
                sections.append(
                    SpectreSpiceSection(
                        language=current_lang,
                        text="\n".join(current_lines) + "\n",
                    )
                )
                current_lines = []
            current_lang = m.group(1).lower()
        else:
            current_lines.append(line)

    if current_lines:
        sections.append(
            SpectreSpiceSection(
                language=current_lang,
                text="\n".join(current_lines) + "\n",
            )
        )

    return sections

class SpiceParser:
    """Parse SPICE/HSPICE netlist text into a Netlist model.

    The Lark parser instance is built once and cached at class level.
    """

    lark_instance: ClassVar[Lark | None] = None

    @classmethod
    def get_lark(cls) -> Lark:
        if cls.lark_instance is None:
            grammar_text = (
                resource_files("kfnetlist.morphnet.netlist.grammars")
                .joinpath("spice.lark")
                .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            )
            cls.lark_instance = Lark(grammar_text, parser="earley", ambiguity="resolve")
        return cls.lark_instance

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Netlist:
        """Parse SPICE netlist text into a Netlist model.

        Steps:
        1. Pre-process: strip comments, join continuations — O(lines)
        2. Lark parse: build parse tree — O(n) with Earley
        3. Transform: convert tree to Circuit models — O(n) with dict lookups
        """
        cleaned = preprocess_spice(text)
        lark = cls.get_lark()
        tree = lark.parse(cleaned)
        transformer = SpiceTransformer()
        return transformer.transform(tree)

def join_continuations(lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """Join SPICE continuation lines (+ at column 0 of the next line)."""
    if not lines:
        return ""
    merged: list[str] = [lines[0]]
    for line in lines[1:]:
        if line.startswith("+"):
            merged[-1] += " " + line[1:].lstrip()
        else:
            merged.append(line)
    return "\n".join(merged)

  1. Strip comment lines (* at column 0) and inline comments ($ or ;).

  3. Collapse runs of whitespace to single spaces, strip trailing whitespace.

def preprocess_spice(text: str) -> str:
    """Prepare SPICE/HSPICE text for Lark parsing.

    1. Strip comment lines (* at column 0) and inline comments ($ or ;).
    2. Join continuation lines (+ at start of next line appends to previous).
    3. Collapse runs of whitespace to single spaces, strip trailing whitespace.
    4. Ensure a trailing newline.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("*"):
            continue
        cleaned = strip_inline_comment(stripped)
        if not cleaned:
            continue
        lines.append(cleaned)

    joined = join_continuations(lines)
    if joined and not joined.endswith("\n"):
        joined += "\n"
    return joined

def strip_inline_comment(line: str) -> str:
    """Remove inline SPICE comments ($ or ;) outside of quoted strings."""
    in_quote = False
    for i, ch in enumerate(line):
        if ch == "'":
            in_quote = not in_quote
        elif not in_quote and ch in ("$", ";"):
            return line[:i].rstrip()
    return line
